```md
# Análise de desempenho

_17/10/2026. As medições abaixo distinguem logs anteriores, teste determinístico novo e trabalho ainda não medido. Nenhum número é atribuído a uma GPU nesta auditoria._

> **Revisão de 17/10 (validação posterior):** o ini de teste desta auditoria (`build/audit-dynamic.ini`) foi escrito com CRLF, e o leitor de `larecomp.ini` só removia o CR de `mod` e `game_lang`: `resolution = dynamic` virou "Automática" e as execuções em jogo descritas abaixo **não tinham resolução dinâmica ligada** (o próprio código antigo também não registra `[dynres]` assim, nem forçado a 20 fps). Refeito com ini LF, mesma rota do Eevee 1.0.0 a 30 fps: código antigo 1,00 → 0,60; código novo entre 0,95 e 1,00 (só reage aos travamentos de carregamento); modo 60 no mundo a 60,49 fps de média. O leitor agora remove CR/LF de toda linha (HISTORICO 56). Prioridade revista: **P3**, porque a resolução dinâmica não aparece no launcher (só `resolution = dynamic` editado à mão).

## Baseline disponível

O renderer registra janelas de aproximadamente 2 s em `runtime/nvn/vulkan/device.c`: fps da janela, maior intervalo, draws, passes, uploads e tempo de compilação. `tools/perf_summary.py` as resume. Nesta auditoria, ao processar logs **preexistentes** (sem repetir a sessão, logo não comparáveis como benchmark):

| Log | Duração | FPS médio das janelas após boot | Janelas com quadro >50 ms | Draws pulados | Programas compilados |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `logs/repro-menu.log` | 52 s | 31,4 | 4/25 | 716 | 473 |
| `logs/repro-link2.log` | 96 s | 30,7 | 6/47 | 514 | 444 |

Uma execução nova, `build/audit-dynamic-world.log` (Eevee 1.0.0, save copiado, 30 fps, resolução dinâmica, janela 1280×720, áudio desligado), chegou ao mundo no present 1450: 48 s, 23 janelas de ~2 s a 30,0 fps, uma janela com quadro máximo de 64 ms, 527 draws pulados em 7 janelas de compilação, 479 programas compilados. Não há linha `[dynres]`, portanto não houve redução registrada da escala. A captura `build/window.png` mostrou a cena 3D. **O áudio não foi testado** nessa execução.

Essas sessões envolvem cenas, compilação e opções diferentes; os números **não** medem o ganho da correção. O parser dá média de janelas, não FPS médio ponderado por quadros. O maior intervalo de cada janela tampouco permite reconstruir percentis.

Foi adicionada coleta opcional por present em `runtime/nvn/vulkan/device.c` (`LARECOMP_FRAMETIME_CSV=<caminho>`), resumida por `tools/frametime_summary.py` com percentis *nearest rank*. Numa execução nova do Eevee, `build/audit-30-frametimes.csv`, filtrando presents 1320–1449 do mundo: **130 amostras, média 33,332 ms (30,00 fps), P95 34,326 ms, P99 43,453 ms, máximo 58,980 ms, um quadro >50 ms**. São intervalos de **presents do jogo**, não tempos de trabalho da GPU. CPU/GPU, RAM e VRAM seguem sem medição.

No trecho 1360–1449, após a entrada do mundo nos dois modos, com o mesmo save copiado e entrada roteirizada:

| Modo | Amostras | Média | P95 | P99 | Máximo | >50 ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 30 fps | 90 | 33,334 ms (30,00 fps) | 33,723 ms | 34,966 ms | 34,966 ms | 0 |
| 60 experimental | 90 | 16,540 ms (60,46 fps) | 18,152 ms | 18,585 ms | 18,585 ms | 0 |

O log do modo 60 marcou `world: 60 fps` no present 1342. As cenas podem estar em tempos de jogo diferentes apesar de terem o mesmo número de presents; a tabela compara **cadência**, não qualidade de gameplay ou ganho de GPU. Não houve linha `[dynres]` em nenhuma das duas execuções. O áudio foi desligado nos testes.

## Gargalos e custos identificados no código

- **Compilação inicial de shaders/pipelines:** `runtime/nvn/vulkan/exec.c` usa workers e orçamento de espera por draw; `renderer_stats()` expõe tradução, SPIR-V, pipelines e draws aguardados. A pesquisa anterior em `docs/HISTORICO.md`, parte 8, mediu pop-in e o efeito do cache. Repetir com cache frio/quente e nas duas GPUs alvo antes de mudar o orçamento.
- **Submissão e sincronização:** `LARECOMP_VK_PROF=1` separa tempo de execução, descriptor sets, cópias de vértices e submit; o log `[hitch]` identifica quadros acima de 50 ms. Não há amostras novas desses contadores nesta auditoria.
- **Resolução dinâmica:** havia decisão incorreta em 30 Hz, que baixava a resolução sem pressão real de desempenho. O ajuste é uma **correção de qualidade e controle**, não uma otimização de FPS.
- **Dispatch e recompilação:** `runtime/dispatch.c` usa cache direto por thread para chamadas indiretas; `runtime/cpu.h` adiciona ramo de profiler/hook em cada entrada. Há custo potencial, mas não foi perfilado, então não cabe substituir por LTO/PGO ou paralelismo especulativo.

## Comparação reproduzível da correção

`tools/test_output_scale.c` chama a implementação real de `output_scale` em 180 presents sintéticos. Compilar contra `git show HEAD:runtime/nvn/output_scale.c` e contra o arquivo alterado isola a lógica de decisão:

| Cenário | Antes | Depois | Critério |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Modo 30, 33,33 ms por present | escala 0,70, teste falha | escala 1,00, teste passa | Não reduzir a resolução com ritmo nominal. |
| Modo 30, 45 ms por present | — | escala 0,70 | Ainda reagir a carga persistente. |
| Modo 60, 16,67 ms por present | — | escala 1,00 | Preservar o comportamento nominal de 60 Hz. |
| Modo 60, 25 ms por present | — | escala 0,70 | Reduzir a escala quando não sustenta 60 Hz. |
| Transição 30→60→30, 90 presents em cada fase nominal | — | escala 1,00 | Não misturar amostras de frequências diferentes. |

Comando do teste: `clang -O2 -Iruntime tools/test_output_scale.c runtime/nvn/output_scale.c -o build/test_output_scale.exe`, seguido de `build/test_output_scale.exe <30|60> <ms>` para os quatro valores e `build/test_output_scale.exe transition`. A escala final 0,70 depende dos 180 quadros e do cooldown atual; o teste verifica a direção da decisão.

## Próxima rodada de profiling

1. Repetir a coleta `LARECOMP_FRAMETIME_CSV` no mesmo trecho de mundo, save, entrada, resolução e cache, separando boot/loading; quantificar overhead do CSV em uma sessão pareada.
2. Em sessões 30 e 60, registrar `LARECOMP_VK_PROF`, `LARECOMP_FNPROF`, estatísticas do renderer, CPU por thread, uso de RAM/VRAM e GPU timestamps. Capturar RenderDoc/Nsight apenas nos quadros lentos; captura contínua altera o ritmo.
3. Comparar cache frio/quente, SMAA ligado/desligado e 1080p/1440p/4K. Só então escolher entre otimizar shaders, descriptor sets, uploads, submits ou sincronização.
4. Rodar o mesmo cenário em Eevee e Pikachu; manter resultados de diferentes máquinas separados.

Não há comparação de FPS antes/depois da correção porque não foi executado benchmark de jogo pareado. O teste isolado comprova a **decisão de escala**; a execução nova verifica que o jogo iniciou e apresentou o mundo sem redução registrada, mas não mede ganho de tempo de GPU.
```

```txt
Let's Go Recomp
===============

A native Windows port of Pokemon: Let's Go, Eevee! and Pikachu! (Nintendo Switch) by static recompilation.
Project page, full documentation and source code: https://github.com/raulzrrs/letsgo-recomp

NO GAME FILES ARE INCLUDED. You need your own legally obtained copy of Pokemon: Let's Go, Eevee! or Pikachu!,
extracted (the exefs and romfs folders).

Supported: Pokemon: Let's Go, Eevee! (title id 0100187003A36000) and Pikachu! (010003F003A34000), any version.
The experimental options below need version 1.0.0 (the base game) of either; Pikachu 1.0.0
was tested up to the name screen of a new game. Cartridge or eShop, any region.
Packed files (.xci, .nsp, .nsz, .nca) must be extracted first.

Requirements
------------
- Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit
- A CPU with AVX2, FMA and BMI2 (Intel Haswell / 2013 or newer, AMD Excavator / Zen or newer); checked at startup
- A GPU whose driver supports Vulkan 1.3 (GPUs that report less are skipped); see vulkan.gpuinfo.org for yours
- RAM: the game used up to 3.8 GB while playing, the one-time setup 5.2 GB (measured). Tested on a 32 GB machine
- About 6 GB of free disk space (measured: 5.7 GB at the peak of the one-time setup, 4.6 GB afterwards)

How to play
-----------
1. Unzip this folder anywhere you can write to (e.g. D:\Games\LetsGoRecomp). Not inside Program Files.
2. Open LetsGoRecomp.exe. It is not code-signed: if Windows says "Windows protected your PC", click "More info"
   and then "Run anyway".
3. Click "Select game folder..." and pick the folder with your extracted game (the one that holds exefs and romfs,
   or any folder above it).
4. Wait while the game files are copied and the game code is recompiled for your PC. This happens only once and
   takes a while (22 minutes measured on a 20-thread CPU, longer with fewer threads).
5. Click Play.

Experimental options (start screen; version 1.0.0 of either game: greyed out for updated games)
- Frame rate limit (Graphics page, also in the F12 menu): 30 (the game's), 60 or 120 fps - the overworld at that rate
  without speed-ups; menus and the Pokedex smoothed; battles and captures stay at 30.
- Wild battles (Game page, off by default): touching a wild Pokemon starts a classic battle against it, then the capture.
The controller stick dead zone is on the Controls page.

Both games: one folder holds one set-up game, so unzip this twice (e.g. LetsGoRecomp-Eevee and LetsGoRecomp-Pikachu)
and set each one up with its game.

Everything stays in this folder: settings (larecomp.ini), saves (save\, or save-pikachu\ for Pikachu), the game files (extracted\), mods and
translations (mods\) and the log (lasrecomp.log). To move or back up the game, move or copy the whole folder.

Translations and mods
---------------------
On the start screen's Mods page, click "Install a mod..." and pick the file you downloaded (.zip, .rar or .7z, as it
came; packs made for Atmosphere / LayeredFS work: translations, textures, models). It comes ticked; several can be on
at once (where two replace the same file, the higher one in the list wins).
Mods of the game's code (exefs, IPS patches, cheats) don't work in this port.

Portugues (Brasil): para jogar em portugues, baixe a traducao PT-BR de fas do grupo Pokemon Switch Brasil, abra a pagina
"Mods", clique em "Instalar mod..." e escolha o arquivo baixado (.rar ou .zip, do jeito que veio). Ela ja vem marcada
na lista.
A traducao substitui os textos em ingles e espanhol: num jogo novo, escolha English ou Espanol na tela de idioma do
jogo. O programa abre em portugues quando o Windows esta em portugues.

Controls
--------
Keyboard: WASD walk, Space/Enter = A, Q/Backspace = B, Tab = X (menu), R = Y, Z/C = L/R, = and - = Plus/Minus,
arrows = D-pad, Esc = close, F12 = settings (volume, image, effects; on a controller: - and + together, then Settings).
All keys can be changed on the start screen.
Mouse: aims Poke Balls (like the Switch's motion controls), left button throws; outside of aiming, the left button is
a finger on the touch screen (Play with your partner). Right button = B.
Controllers: any controller SDL recognizes (Xbox, PlayStation, Switch Pro...), handheld-mode layout. The right stick
plus ZR is a finger on the touch screen.

Troubleshooting
---------------
- "Not Pokemon: Let's Go, Eevee! or Pikachu!": pick the folder of your own extracted game.
- Packed game files (.xci / .nsp) must be extracted first.
- "The game code builder is missing": your antivirus may have quarantined lasgen\lasgen.exe (a PyInstaller
  program, sometimes flagged by mistake). Restore it or add this folder as an exception.
- The game closes or doesn't start: see lasrecomp.log in this folder and report it on the project page.

Legal
-----
Fan project, not affiliated with Nintendo, The Pokemon Company, Game Freak or Creatures. MIT licensed (LICENSE.txt),
based on LAS Recomp by Peiikai (LICENSE-LASRecomp.txt, https://github.com/peiikai/LASRecomp).
Bundled: SDL3 (zlib), FFmpeg (LGPL 2.1, built with only the decoders the game needs; source: https://ffmpeg.org),
shaderc (Apache 2.0), libiconv (LGPL), Zig (MIT), the Baloo 2 font (SIL OFL 1.1, Baloo2-OFL.txt),
AMD's FidelityFX SDK runtime for FSR 3.1 (MIT, amd_fidelityfx_vk.dll, FidelityFX-LICENSE.txt), and the
GCC / MinGW-w64 runtime libraries (GPL with the runtime library exception).
```

`docs/technical-audit.md`:

```md
# Auditoria técnica do port nativo

_17/10/2026. Escopo: revisão estática dos caminhos críticos do runtime e do gerador, pesquisa já reproduzida neste repositório, compilação do runtime e teste isolado da resolução dinâmica. Não é uma prova de correção de todas as instruções ARM64, serviços ou cenas._

> **Revisão de 17/10 (validação posterior):** o ini de teste desta auditoria (`build/audit-dynamic.ini`) foi escrito com CRLF, e o leitor de `larecomp.ini` só removia o CR de `mod` e `game_lang`: `resolution = dynamic` virou "Automática" e as execuções em jogo descritas abaixo **não tinham resolução dinâmica ligada** (o próprio código antigo também não registra `[dynres]` assim, nem forçado a 20 fps). Refeito com ini LF, mesma rota do Eevee 1.0.0 a 30 fps: código antigo 1,00 → 0,60; código novo entre 0,95 e 1,00 (só reage aos travamentos de carregamento); modo 60 no mundo a 60,49 fps de média. O leitor agora remove CR/LF de toda linha (HISTORICO 56). Prioridade revista: **P3**, porque a resolução dinâmica não aparece no launcher (só `resolution = dynamic` editado à mão).

## Arquitetura observada

`tools/gen.py`, `analyze.py`, `lifter.py` e `patches.py` convertem os quatro NSO em C; `Makefile` compila o resultado em `lasgame.dll` com `-O1`, `-fno-strict-aliasing` e `-march=x86-64-v3`. `runtime/loader.c` carrega os segmentos, símbolos e relocations no espaço de endereços do guest. `runtime/cpu.h` mantém registradores gerais, vetoriais, flags, FPCR/FPSR e helpers de memória/atômicos. `runtime/dispatch.c` resolve chamadas indiretas por tabelas ordenadas com cache por thread. `runtime/fnhook.c` permite interceptar funções do jogo sem editar C gerado, traduzindo endereços conhecidos do Eevee 1.0.0 para o Pikachu 1.0.0.

O runtime implementa kernel e IPC (`runtime/kernel.c`, `ipc.c`), serviços (`runtime/services/`), entrada e vídeo (`runtime/hle/`) e NVN (`runtime/nvn/`). O backend Vulkan traduz comandos NVN, shaders Maxwell e recursos; shaders e pipelines são compilados em workers (`runtime/nvn/vulkan/exec.c`). O jogo mantém a lógica; o runtime controla o ritmo de apresentação em `runtime/nvn/objects.c`.

## Descobertas priorizadas

| Prioridade | Evidência | Consequência e ação |
|---|---|---|
| **P3 corrigido** | `runtime/nvn/output_scale.c`: `dyn_update` usava limiares de 17,4 ms e 14,5 ms para qualquer cena; `runtime/nvn/objects.c` usa ~33,3 ms no modo padrão. | Resolução dinâmica podia cair de 1,00 para 0,50 em 30 fps estáveis. Limiares agora usam 33,33 ms em cenas de 30 Hz e 16,67 ms no mundo/menu do modo 60, descartando amostras de uma frequência ao trocar de cena. Teste determinístico: 180 quadros a 33,33 ms resultavam em 0,70 antes e 1,00 depois. |
| **P1 em investigação** | `runtime/dispatch.c:hle_unimplemented` devolve `x0=0` a símbolos sem HLE; `runtime/ipc.c` também tem serviços offline. | Alguns chamadores podem interpretar sucesso e tentar usar um objeto ausente. Inventariar símbolos/serviços usados por Eevee e Pikachu com `LARECOMP_TRACE_SVC` e logs `[hle] UNIMPLEMENTED`; implementar resultado correto por contrato do SDK. A presença do stub, isoladamente, não prova falha em gameplay. |
| **P2 em investigação** | `runtime/hle/fps60.c:accessor_hook` escreve temporariamente `G[1]` em memória compartilhada, chama o guest e restaura. | Um leitor em outra thread pode observar 16,67 ms durante a janela do hook. Medir leitores e threads antes de substituir por valor local no objeto de temporizadores. Nenhuma corrida foi reproduzida nesta auditoria. |
| **P2 em investigação** | `runtime/nvn/vulkan/exec.c` mantém objetos antigos `Prog`/`Pipe` para evitar colisão de chaves por ponteiro, conforme comentário próximo ao cache. | Uso de memória pode crescer com recriações de programas. Medir número de objetos, bytes e duração de sessões longas; trocar a identidade por geração/ID só depois de validar todas as chaves. |
| **P2 em investigação** | `runtime/cpu.h` faz stores comuns diretamente e implementa exclusivos com `__atomic_*`; `tools/lifter.py` emite fence para barreiras. | Falta uma prova diferencial ampla para semântica de atomics, NEON e FPCR/FPSR sob concorrência. Priorizar corpus de instruções e comparação com execução ARM64 legítima; não converter código compartilhado por threads sem essa prova. |
| **P2 em investigação** | `runtime/nvn/vulkan/exec.c:vk_full_barrier` usa `ALL_COMMANDS`/`MEMORY_WRITE` em diversos pontos entre passes, cópias e dispatches. | Uma barreira ampla pode serializar trabalho da GPU, mas a segurança de reduzi-la depende do produtor/consumidor de cada recurso. Capturar GPU timestamps e validação Vulkan antes de especializar; não há ganho medido aqui. |

O risco do cache de programas e o de leitura concorrente de `G[1]` são **hipóteses sustentadas pelo código**, ainda sem reprodução de defeito. Não foram tratados como bugs confirmados.

## Cobertura da revisão estática

| Área | Evidência conferida | Limite da conclusão |
|---|---|---|
| Mapeamento e branches indiretos | `tools/analyze.py` extrai inícios de `.eh_frame_hdr` e ponteiros de código em dados; `tools/lifter.py` distingue `blr`/`br`; `runtime/dispatch.c` resolve endereços com busca e cache. | Não foi feito teste diferencial de todas as jump tables e targets contra ARM64. |
| Estado da CPU, SIMD e FP | `runtime/cpu.h` fixa offsets com `_Static_assert`; `tools/simd_c.py`, `runtime/simd.h`/`simd_fp.h` tratam FPCR, NaN, FZ e FMA com caminhos lentos. | A presença de tratamento não prova equivalência bit a bit; faltam vetores de referência para arredondamento, flags e casos extremos. |
| Kernel, serviços, filesystem, áudio e input | `runtime/kernel.c` usa mutex/condvar e implementa semântica de timeout documentada; `runtime/services/`, `runtime/hle/input.c` e `movie.c` cobrem os caminhos do jogo observados no histórico. | Nesta rodada não houve carga concorrente, teste de save/load, áudio habilitado ou varredura completa de códigos de retorno. |
| Vulkan | `exec.c` mantém cache de pipelines, workers, descriptor pools, ring transitório e barriers; `textures.c` contém caminhos de staging e conversão. | Não houve captura RenderDoc/validação nem perfil de stalls, overdraw, VRAM ou custo de barriers. |

## Estratégia de regressão

Para testes roteirizados, `tools/repro.sh` copia o save para `build/test-save` e usa `LARECOMP_INPUT`; ele **apaga** a pasta temporária e `build/frames`, então conferir esses locais antes de executá-lo. Usar `TURBO=0` para medir ritmo real. Testar cada cena nas duas builds 1.0.0, com modo 30 e 60 desligado/ligado conforme aplicável. Comparar quadros correspondentes por tempo de jogo, não apenas por número de presents.

| Cenário | Verificação necessária |
|---|---|
| Inicialização e menus | Boot sem `[hle] UNIMPLEMENTED` novo; seleção, Pokédex e animações na velocidade original. |
| Criação, save/load | Nome correto; save em cópia; recarregar e conferir integridade. |
| Mundo, NPCs e transições | Posição, câmera, diálogo, fade, objetos e ausência de draws pulados após carregamento. |
| Batalha e captura | Turnos, animações, mira, anel e timers; 60 experimental deve manter a velocidade do modo 30. |
| Áudio e vídeo | Sem underrun; sincronismo com quadro e com tempo de parede. |
| 1080p, 1440p, 4K | Captura da imagem interna e da janela, viewport, profundidade, UI, sombras e pós-processamento. |
| Resolução dinâmica | Em 30 Hz estáveis, escala deve ficar em 1,00; sob carga persistente deve cair; repetir ao entrar/sair do modo 60. |

Nesta execução houve build do runtime, teste isolado e execuções roteirizadas do **Eevee 1.0.0** em 30 e 60 experimental, com `resolution = dynamic`, save copiado para `build/audit-save-20261017` e áudio desligado. Ambas chegaram ao mundo e produziram captura de cena 3D em 1280×720, sem linha `[dynres]`. A instrumentação opcional mediu, nos 90 presents 1360–1449, médias de 33,334 ms (30) e 16,540 ms (60); detalhes em `performance-analysis.md`. **Pikachu, áudio, alternância de cenas, velocidade do gameplay e testes manuais não foram validados**; uma release exige essas etapas. `tools/test_output_scale.c` cobre a decisão de escala, não toda a apresentação Vulkan.
```

```md
# Fontes do sistema (opcional)

Parte dos textos do jogo usa a fonte embutida no sistema do Switch, que não faz parte dos arquivos do jogo. Sem ela,
o Let's Go Recomp usa a Yu Gothic do Windows (o mesmo estilo de gótico japonês da Morisawa UD Shin Go do Switch) e,
na falta dela, a Arial. A maior parte do jogo desenha os textos com as fontes do próprio romfs e não muda.

Para o visual exato, coloque aqui uma cópia tirada do **seu** console (arquivos de sistema *FontStandard*,
título 0100000000000811, e *FontNintendoExtension*, 0100000000000810):

- `nintendo_udsg-r_std_003.bfttf`: a fonte principal (um `.ttf` com o mesmo nome, ou escrito `nintendo_udsgr_std_003`,
  também serve)
- `nintendo_ext_003.bfttf`: os símbolos dos botões (opcional)

`LARECOMP_FONT=<arquivo>` passa por cima de tudo (.ttf / .otf / .ttc / .bfttf).

Essas fontes são propriedade da Nintendo: ficam fora do git (`.gitignore`) e nunca devem ser compartilhadas.
```

`runtime/cpu.h`:

```h
// Guest CPU state and helpers used by recompiled code.
#pragma once
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <string.h>

typedef struct __attribute__((aligned(16))) Cpu {
    uint64_t x[32];          // x0-x30 (x[31] unused; sp is separate)
    uint64_t sp;             // 256
    uint64_t pc;             // 264: target for indirect dispatch
    uint64_t nzcv;           // 272: flags in bits 31..28
    uint64_t tpidr;          // 280
    uint64_t tpidrro;        // 288
    uint64_t excl_addr;      // 296
    uint64_t excl_val;       // 304
    void *thread;            // 312: runtime thread object
    uint64_t fpcr;           // 320: guest FPCR/FPSR (portable FP/SIMD lowering only; the asm path uses the host's)
    uint64_t fpsr;           // 328
    uint8_t _pad[512 - 336];
    __uint128_t v[32];       // 512
} Cpu;

_Static_assert(offsetof(Cpu, sp) == 256, "sp");
_Static_assert(offsetof(Cpu, pc) == 264, "pc");
_Static_assert(offsetof(Cpu, nzcv) == 272, "nzcv");
_Static_assert(offsetof(Cpu, fpcr) == 320, "fpcr");
_Static_assert(offsetof(Cpu, fpsr) == 328, "fpsr");
_Static_assert(offsetof(Cpu, v) == 512, "v");

typedef void (*GuestFn)(Cpu *);

// ---- runtime services (runtime/*.c)
void rt_dispatch(Cpu *c);                 // call function at c->pc
void rt_svc(Cpu *c, uint32_t imm, uint64_t pc);
void rt_brk(Cpu *c, uint32_t imm, uint64_t pc) __attribute__((noreturn));
void rt_udf(Cpu *c, uint64_t pc) __attribute__((noreturn));
uint64_t rt_ticks(void);

#if defined(__aarch64__)
static inline uint64_t rt_get_fpcr(void) { uint64_t v; __asm__ volatile("mrs %0, fpcr" : "=r"(v)); return v; }
static inline uint64_t rt_get_fpsr(void) { uint64_t v; __asm__ volatile("mrs %0, fpsr" : "=r"(v)); return v; }
static inline void rt_set_fpcr(uint64_t v) { __asm__ volatile("msr fpcr, %0" :: "r"(v)); }
static inline void rt_set_fpsr(uint64_t v) { __asm__ volatile("msr fpsr, %0" :: "r"(v)); }
#else
// Host FP state is not the guest's here: code lifted with --simd=c keeps FPCR/FPSR in Cpu (c->fpcr, zeroed
// with the Cpu), so the host-side reset in thread start-up has nothing to do.
static inline uint64_t rt_get_fpcr(void) { return 0; }
static inline uint64_t rt_get_fpsr(void) { return 0; }
static inline void rt_set_fpcr(uint64_t v) { (void)v; }
static inline void rt_set_fpsr(uint64_t v) { (void)v; }
#endif

// ---- memory: guest addresses are host addresses
typedef uint16_t __attribute__((aligned(1), may_alias)) u16u;
typedef uint32_t __attribute__((aligned(1), may_alias)) u32u;
typedef uint64_t __attribute__((aligned(1), may_alias)) u64u;
typedef uint8_t __attribute__((may_alias)) u8a;

// Function-entry profiler (runtime/fnprof.c, LARECOMP_FNPROF): one predictable branch per call when off.
// Function hooks (runtime/fnhook.c): while any is registered, rt_fnhook may handle the call (returns 1: the guest
// function returns at once, with the registers the hook left).
extern volatile int g_fnprof;
void fnprof_hit(uint64_t addr, uint64_t lr, uint64_t x0);
extern volatile int g_fnhook;
int rt_fnhook(Cpu *c, uint64_t addr);
#define FN_ENTER(a) do {                                                             \
        if (__builtin_expect(g_fnprof, 0)) fnprof_hit(a, c->x[30], c->x[0]);         \
        if (__builtin_expect(g_fnhook, 0) && rt_fnhook(c, a)) return;                \
    } while (0)

#define LD8(a)  (*(const u8a *)(uintptr_t)(a))
#define LD16(a) (*(const u16u *)(uintptr_t)(a))
#define LD32(a) (*(const u32u *)(uintptr_t)(a))
#define LD64(a) (*(const u64u *)(uintptr_t)(a))
#define ST8(a, v)  (*(u8a *)(uintptr_t)(a) = (uint8_t)(v))
#define ST16(a, v) (*(u16u *)(uintptr_t)(a) = (uint16_t)(v))
#define ST32(a, v) (*(u32u *)(uintptr_t)(a) = (uint32_t)(v))
#define ST64(a, v) (*(u64u *)(uintptr_t)(a) = (uint64_t)(v))
// Research build (gen.py --trace-stores, -DSTORE_TRACE): the generated stores are ST<N>T(<guest pc>, a, v) and report
// (pc, address, old, new) to the runtime (runtime/storetrace.c); otherwise exactly ST<N>.
#ifdef STORE_TRACE
void rt_trace_store(uint64_t pc, uint64_t addr, uint64_t old, uint64_t nw, int size);
#define ST_TRACED(T, pc, a, v, N) do { T _o = *(T *)(uintptr_t)(a); T _n = (T)(v); *(T *)(uintptr_t)(a) = _n; if (_o != _n) rt_trace_store((pc), (uint64_t)(a), _o, _n, N); } while (0)
#define ST8T(pc, a, v)  ST_TRACED(uint8_t, pc, a, v, 1)
#define ST16T(pc, a, v) ST_TRACED(uint16_t, pc, a, v, 2)
#define ST32T(pc, a, v) ST_TRACED(uint32_t, pc, a, v, 4)
#define ST64T(pc, a, v) ST_TRACED(uint64_t, pc, a, v, 8)
#else
#define ST8T(pc, a, v)  ST8(a, v)
#define ST16T(pc, a, v) ST16(a, v)
#define ST32T(pc, a, v) ST32(a, v)
#define ST64T(pc, a, v) ST64(a, v)
#endif

// ---- exclusive monitor (emulated with compare-and-swap)
#define EXCL(N, T)                                                                         \
    static inline uint64_t ldx##N(Cpu *c, uint64_t a) {                                    \
        T v = __atomic_load_n((T *)(uintptr_t)a, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);                        \
        c->excl_addr = a;                                                                  \
        c->excl_val = v;                                                                   \
        return v;                                                                          \
    }                                                                                      \
    static inline uint32_t stx##N(Cpu *c, uint64_t a, uint64_t v) {                        \
        if (c->excl_addr != a) return 1;                                                   \
        c->excl_addr = ~0ull;                                                              \
        T expected = (T)c->excl_val;                                                       \
        return !__atomic_compare_exchange_n((T *)(uintptr_t)a, &expected, (T)v, 0,         \
                                            __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST, __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST);           \
    }                                                                                      \
    static inline uint64_t lda##N(uint64_t a) {                                            \
        return __atomic_load_n((T *)(uintptr_t)a, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);                       \
    }                                                                                      \
    static inline void stl##N(uint64_t a, uint64_t v) {                                    \
        __atomic_store_n((T *)(uintptr_t)a, (T)v, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);                       \
    }
EXCL(8, uint8_t)
EXCL(16, uint16_t)
EXCL(32, uint32_t)
EXCL(64, uint64_t)

// ---- flags (packed NZCV in bits 31..28)
#define FLAG_N(c) (((c)->nzcv >> 31) & 1)
#define FLAG_Z(c) (((c)->nzcv >> 30) & 1)
#define FLAG_C(c) (((c)->nzcv >> 29) & 1)
#define FLAG_V(c) (((c)->nzcv >> 28) & 1)
#define COND_EQ(c) (FLAG_Z(c))
#define COND_NE(c) (!FLAG_Z(c))
#define COND_CS(c) (FLAG_C(c))
#define COND_CC(c) (!FLAG_C(c))
#define COND_MI(c) (FLAG_N(c))
#define COND_PL(c) (!FLAG_N(c))
#define COND_VS(c) (FLAG_V(c))
#define COND_VC(c) (!FLAG_V(c))
#define COND_HI(c) (FLAG_C(c) && !FLAG_Z(c))
#define COND_LS(c) (!(FLAG_C(c) && !FLAG_Z(c)))
#define COND_GE(c) (FLAG_N(c) == FLAG_V(c))
#define COND_LT(c) (FLAG_N(c) != FLAG_V(c))
#define COND_GT(c) (!FLAG_Z(c) && FLAG_N(c) == FLAG_V(c))
#define COND_LE(c) (!(!FLAG_Z(c) && FLAG_N(c) == FLAG_V(c)))

#define MKFLAGS(n, z, cy, v) \
    (((uint64_t)(n) << 31) | ((uint64_t)(z) << 30) | ((uint64_t)(cy) << 29) | ((uint64_t)(v) << 28))

static inline uint64_t adds64(Cpu *c, uint64_t a, uint64_t b) {
    uint64_t r = a + b;
    c->nzcv = MKFLAGS(r >> 63, r == 0, r < a, ((a ^ r) & (b ^ r)) >> 63);
    return r;
}
static inline uint64_t subs64(Cpu *c, uint64_t a, uint64_t b) {
    uint64_t r = a - b;
    c->nzcv = MKFLAGS(r >> 63, r == 0, a >= b, ((a ^ b) & (a ^ r)) >> 63);
    return r;
}
static inline uint32_t adds32(Cpu *c, uint32_t a, uint32_t b) {
    uint32_t r = a + b;
    c->nzcv = MKFLAGS(r >> 31, r == 0, r < a, ((a ^ r) & (b ^ r)) >> 31);
    return r;
}
static inline uint32_t subs32(Cpu *c, uint32_t a, uint32_t b) {
    uint32_t r = a - b;
    c->nzcv = MKFLAGS(r >> 31, r == 0, a >= b, ((a ^ b) & (a ^ r)) >> 31);
    return r;
}
static inline uint64_t logic64(Cpu *c, uint64_t r) { c->nzcv = MKFLAGS(r >> 63, r == 0, 0, 0); return r; }
static inline uint32_t logic32(Cpu *c, uint32_t r) { c->nzcv = MKFLAGS(r >> 31, r == 0, 0, 0); return r; }

#define ADC_IMPL(N, S)                                                                     \
    static inline uint##N##_t adc##N(Cpu *c, uint##N##_t a, uint##N##_t b) {               \
        return a + b + (uint##N##_t)FLAG_C(c);                                             \
    }                                                                                      \
    static inline uint##N##_t sbc##N(Cpu *c, uint##N##_t a, uint##N##_t b) {               \
        return a - b - 1 + (uint##N##_t)FLAG_C(c);                                         \
    }                                                                                      \
    static inline uint##N##_t adcs##N(Cpu *c, uint##N##_t a, uint##N##_t b) {              \
        uint##N##_t cin = FLAG_C(c), r = a + b + cin;                                      \
        int carry = cin ? r <= a : r < a;                                                  \
        c->nzcv = MKFLAGS(r >> (N - 1), r == 0, carry, ((a ^ r) & (b ^ r)) >> (N - 1));    \
        return r;                                                                          \
    }                                                                                      \
    static inline uint##N##_t sbcs##N(Cpu *c, uint##N##_t a, uint##N##_t b) {              \
        return adcs##N(c, a, (uint##N##_t)~b);                                             \
    }
ADC_IMPL(64, )
ADC_IMPL(32, )

// ---- bit ops
#define ROR64(v, r) ((uint64_t)(v) >> ((r) & 63) | (uint64_t)(v) << ((64 - ((r) & 63)) & 63))
#define ROR32(v, r) ((uint32_t)(v) >> ((r) & 31) | (uint32_t)(v) << ((32 - ((r) & 31)) & 31))
static inline uint64_t clz64(uint64_t v) { return v ? __builtin_clzll(v) : 64; }
static inline uint32_t clz32(uint32_t v) { return v ? __builtin_clz(v) : 32; }
static inline uint64_t cls64(uint64_t v) { return clz64(v ^ (uint64_t)((int64_t)v >> 1)) - 1; }
static inline uint32_t cls32(uint32_t v) { return clz32(v ^ (uint32_t)((int32_t)v >> 1)) - 1; }
static inline uint64_t rbit64(uint64_t v) { return __builtin_bitreverse64(v); }
static inline uint32_t rbit32(uint32_t v) { return __builtin_bitreverse32(v); }
static inline uint32_t rev16_32(uint32_t v) { return ((v & 0x00ff00ffu) << 8) | ((v >> 8) & 0x00ff00ffu); }
static inline uint64_t rev16_64(uint64_t v) {
    return ((v & 0x00ff00ff00ff00ffull) << 8) | ((v >> 8) & 0x00ff00ff00ff00ffull);
}
static inline uint64_t rev32_64(uint64_t v) {
    return ((uint64_t)__builtin_bswap32((uint32_t)v)) | ((uint64_t)__builtin_bswap32((uint32_t)(v >> 32)) << 32);
}
static inline uint64_t udiv64(uint64_t a, uint64_t b) { return b ? a / b : 0; }
static inline uint32_t udiv32(uint32_t a, uint32_t b) { return b ? a / b : 0; }
static inline uint64_t sdiv64(uint64_t a, uint64_t b) {
    if (!b) return 0;
    if ((int64_t)a == INT64_MIN && (int64_t)b == -1) return a;
    return (uint64_t)((int64_t)a / (int64_t)b);
}
static inline uint32_t sdiv32(uint32_t a, uint32_t b) {
    if (!b) return 0;
    if ((int32_t)a == INT32_MIN && (int32_t)b == -1) return a;
    return (uint32_t)((int32_t)a / (int32_t)b);
}

// Portable FP/SIMD helpers for code lifted with --simd=c (default off AArch64; gen.py includes simd.h itself
// in that mode, so AArch64 hosts can build it too).
#if !defined(__cplusplus) && !defined(__aarch64__)
#include "simd.h"
#endif
```

`runtime/dispatch.c`:

```c
// Guest address -> recompiled function lookup, and host (HLE) function registry.
#include <pthread.h>
#include <signal.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <unistd.h>

#include "gamelib.h"
#include "hle.h"

typedef struct { const uint64_t *addrs; const GuestFn *fns; uint64_t count, lo, hi; } FnTable;
static FnTable tables[GAMELIB_MAX_MODULES];
static int ntables;

// HLE stubs live at fake addresses HLE_BASE + 16*i
#define MAX_HLE 4096
typedef struct { const char *name; HostFn fn; } HleSlot;
static HleSlot hle_slots[MAX_HLE];
static int hle_count;

// Overrides of recompiled guest functions (by address)
#define MAX_OVERRIDE 1024
static struct { uint64_t addr; HostFn fn; const char *name; } overrides[MAX_OVERRIDE];
static int override_count;

// Host implementations registered by name (runtime/hle/*.c fill this via HLE_FUNC)
typedef struct { const char *name; HostFn fn; } HleImpl;
#ifdef __APPLE__
extern const HleImpl __start_hle_impls[] __asm__("section$start$__DATA$__hle_impls");
extern const HleImpl __stop_hle_impls[] __asm__("section$end$__DATA$__hle_impls");
#elif defined(__linux__)
extern const HleImpl __start_hle_impls[], __stop_hle_impls[];  // (ELF: defined by the linker)
#else
// PE/COFF: the linker sorts .hle$a < .hle$m (entries, hle.h) < .hle$z by the text after '$'.
__attribute__((section(".hle$a"), used)) static const HleImpl __start_hle_impls[1];
__attribute__((section(".hle$z"), used)) static const HleImpl __stop_hle_impls[1];
#endif

HostFn hle_lookup_impl(const char *name) {
    const char *skip = getenv("LARECOMP_HLE_SKIP");  // debugging: disable HLE for names containing this
    if (skip && strstr(name, skip)) return NULL;
    const HleImpl *start = __start_hle_impls, *stop = __stop_hle_impls;
    __asm__("" : "+r"(start), "+r"(stop));  // separate objects: keep the compiler from reasoning about them
    for (const HleImpl *p = start; p < stop; p++)
        if (p->name && !strcmp(p->name, name)) return p->fn;
    return NULL;
}

static void hle_unimplemented(Cpu *c);

uint64_t hle_register(const char *name, HostFn fn) {
    for (int i = 0; i < hle_count; i++)
        if (!strcmp(hle_slots[i].name, name)) return HLE_BASE + 16ull * i;
    if (hle_count == MAX_HLE) FATAL("too many HLE stubs\n");
    hle_slots[hle_count].name = strdup(name);
    hle_slots[hle_count].fn = fn;
    {   // LARECOMP_HLE_WHO=<fake address, hex>[,...]: names the host function behind an address of a thread dump
        const char *who = getenv("LARECOMP_HLE_WHO");
        char want[32];
        snprintf(want, sizeof want, "%llx", (unsigned long long)(HLE_BASE + 16ull * hle_count));
        if (who && strstr(who, want)) LOG("[hle] %s = %s%s\n", want, name, fn ? "" : " (no host implementation)");
    }
    return HLE_BASE + 16ull * hle_count++;
}

void hle_override(uint64_t addr, HostFn fn, const char *name) {
    if (override_count == MAX_OVERRIDE) FATAL("too many overrides\n");
    overrides[override_count].addr = addr;
    overrides[override_count].fn = fn;
    overrides[override_count].name = name;
    override_count++;
}

// ---- recent-HLE ring (crash debugging: what the game asked the host just before dying)
#define HHIST 128
static __thread struct { const char *name; uint64_t x0, x1, x30; } hhist[HHIST];
static __thread int hhist_n;
static void hhist_push(const char *name, Cpu *c) {
    int i = hhist_n++ & (HHIST - 1);
    hhist[i].name = name;
    hhist[i].x0 = c->x[0];
    hhist[i].x1 = c->x[1];
    hhist[i].x30 = c->x[30];
}
static void hhist_dump(void) {
    int n = hhist_n < HHIST ? hhist_n : HHIST, start = hhist_n - n;
    fprintf(stderr, "last %d host calls:\n", n);
    for (int k = 0; k < n; k++) {
        int i = (start + k) & (HHIST - 1);
        fprintf(stderr, "  %s x0=%llx x1=%llx lr=%llx\n", hhist[i].name ? hhist[i].name : "?",
                (unsigned long long)hhist[i].x0, (unsigned long long)hhist[i].x1, (unsigned long long)hhist[i].x30);
    }
}

static __thread uint64_t unimpl_pc;
static int unimpl_counts[MAX_HLE];
static void hle_unimplemented(Cpu *c) {
    int i = (int)((unimpl_pc - HLE_BASE) / 16);
    if (unimpl_counts[i]++ < 3)
        LOG("[hle] UNIMPLEMENTED %s (x0=%llx x1=%llx lr=%llx) -> returning 0\n", hle_slots[i].name, c->x[0],
            c->x[1], c->x[30]);
    c->x[0] = 0;
}

uint64_t guest_sym(const char *name) {
    // small cache: callers pass string literals, so pointer identity is a good key
    static struct { const char *name; uint64_t addr; } cache[64];
    static pthread_mutex_t m = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;
    pthread_mutex_lock(&m);
    for (int i = 0; i < 64 && cache[i].name; i++)
        if (cache[i].name == name) { uint64_t a = cache[i].addr; pthread_mutex_unlock(&m); return a; }
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&m);
    uint64_t a = loader_find_symbol(name);
    if (!a) FATAL("guest symbol %s not found\n", name);
    pthread_mutex_lock(&m);
    for (int i = 0; i < 64; i++) if (!cache[i].name) { cache[i].name = name; cache[i].addr = a; break; }
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&m);
    return a;
}

static uint64_t hle_next = HLE_HEAP;
RT_ON_RESET(hle_heap_reset) { hle_next = HLE_HEAP; }  // (guest memory, wiped by the reboot)

void *hle_alloc(uint64_t size) {
    static pthread_mutex_t m = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;
    pthread_mutex_lock(&m);
    uint64_t a = hle_next;
    hle_next += (size + 63) & ~63ull;
    if (hle_next > HLE_HEAP + HLE_HEAP_SIZE) FATAL("HLE heap exhausted\n");
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&m);
    plat_commit(a, size);
    memset((void *)a, 0, size);
    return (void *)a;
}

void dispatch_init(void) {  // (after gamelib_load)
    const GameLibTables *g = gamelib_tables();
    ntables = 0;
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < g->nmods && i < GAMELIB_MAX_MODULES; i++) {
        const GameLibModule *m = &g->mods[i];
        uint64_t n = *m->count;
        if (n) tables[ntables++] = (FnTable){m->addrs, m->fns, n, m->addrs[0], m->addrs[n - 1]};
    }
}

GuestFn dispatch_lookup(uint64_t addr) {
    for (int t = 0; t < ntables; t++) {
        FnTable *ft = &tables[t];
        if (addr < ft->lo || addr > ft->hi) continue;
        uint64_t lo = 0, hi = ft->count;
        while (lo < hi) {
            uint64_t mid = (lo + hi) / 2;
            if (ft->addrs[mid] < addr) lo = mid + 1;
            else hi = mid;
        }
        if (lo < ft->count && ft->addrs[lo] == addr) return ft->fns[lo];
    }
    return NULL;
}

// Small direct-mapped cache in front of the binary search
#define DCACHE 4096
static __thread struct { uint64_t addr; GuestFn fn; } dcache[DCACHE];

static GuestFn dispatch_slow(Cpu *c) {
    uint64_t pc = c->pc;
    if (pc >= HLE_BASE && pc < HLE_BASE + HLE_SIZE) {
        rt_unwind_point();  // (HLE calls aren't cached below, so every one passes here: a reboot's safe point)
        int i = (int)((pc - HLE_BASE) / 16);
        if (i < hle_count) {
            hhist_push(hle_slots[i].name, c);
            if (hle_slots[i].fn) return hle_slots[i].fn;
            unimpl_pc = pc;
            return hle_unimplemented;
        }
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < override_count; i++)
        if (overrides[i].addr == pc) return overrides[i].fn;
    GuestFn f = dispatch_lookup(pc);
    if (!f) {
        uint64_t off;
        const char *s = loader_symbol_at(c->x[30], &off);
        FATAL("no function at %llx (lr=%llx %s+%llx)\n", pc, c->x[30], s ? s : "?", off);
    }
    unsigned h = (unsigned)(pc >> 2) & (DCACHE - 1);
    dcache[h].addr = pc;
    dcache[h].fn = f;
    return f;
}

// Always tail-calls, so chains of indirect jumps don't grow the host stack.
void rt_dispatch(Cpu *c) {
    unsigned h = (unsigned)(c->pc >> 2) & (DCACHE - 1);
    GuestFn f = dcache[h].addr == c->pc ? dcache[h].fn : dispatch_slow(c);
    __attribute__((musttail)) return f(c);
}

void guest_call(Cpu *c, uint64_t addr) {
    uint64_t lr = c->x[30];
    c->x[30] = 0;
    c->pc = addr;
    rt_dispatch(c);
    c->x[30] = lr;
}

// Host pc -> recompiled guest function containing it ("f_<addr>"), for hosts without symbol lookup.
static int cmp_host(const void *a, const void *b) {
    uint64_t x = ((const uint64_t *)a)[0], y = ((const uint64_t *)b)[0];
    return x < y ? -1 : x > y;
}
const char *rt_host_fn_name(uint64_t pc, uint64_t *offset) {
    static uint64_t (*byhost)[2];  // {host address, guest address}, sorted by host address
    static uint64_t n;
    static __thread char name[32];
    if (!byhost) {
        uint64_t total = 0, k = 0;
        for (int t = 0; t < ntables; t++) total += tables[t].count;
        uint64_t (*v)[2] = malloc(total * sizeof *v);
        if (!v) return NULL;
        for (int t = 0; t < ntables; t++)
            for (uint64_t i = 0; i < tables[t].count; i++) {
                v[k][0] = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)tables[t].fns[i];
                v[k++][1] = tables[t].addrs[i];
            }
        qsort(v, k, sizeof *v, cmp_host);
        n = k;
        byhost = v;
    }
    uint64_t lo = 0, hi = n;  // last entry with host address <= pc
    while (lo < hi) {
        uint64_t mid = (lo + hi) / 2;
        if (byhost[mid][0] <= pc) lo = mid + 1;
        else hi = mid;
    }
    if (!lo || pc - byhost[lo - 1][0] > 0x100000) return NULL;
    snprintf(name, sizeof name, "f_%llx", (unsigned long long)byhost[lo - 1][1]);
    if (offset) *offset = pc - byhost[lo - 1][0];
    return name;
}

static const char *host_sym(uint64_t pc, uint64_t *offset) {
    // (game functions first: they live in lasgame.dll, which the OS lookup can only name as a whole)
    const char *s = rt_host_fn_name(pc, offset);
    return s ? s : plat_symbol(pc, offset);
}

void rt_fatal_trace(void) {
    hhist_dump();
    fprintf(stderr, "host backtrace (guest functions are f_<addr>):\n");
    plat_print_backtrace();
    Cpu *c = kernel_current_cpu();
    if (c) {
        fprintf(stderr, "guest: sp=%llx lr=%llx\n", c->sp, c->x[30]);
        for (int i = 0; i < 31; i += 4)
            fprintf(stderr, "  x%-2d %016llx  x%-2d %016llx  x%-2d %016llx  x%-2d %016llx\n", i, c->x[i], i + 1,
                    c->x[i + 1], i + 2, c->x[i + 2], i + 3, c->x[i + 3]);
    }
    plat_fatal_notice();
    // our crash handler also catches SIGABRT: without this abort() re-entered it forever (a 5 GB log)
    signal(SIGABRT, SIG_DFL);
    abort();
}

void rt_udf(Cpu *c, uint64_t pc) {
    (void)c;
    FATAL("undefined instruction / trap at %llx\n", pc);
}

void rt_brk(Cpu *c, uint32_t imm, uint64_t pc) {
    (void)c;
    FATAL("brk #%u at %llx\n", imm, pc);
}

// ---- crash reporting

// Debug data watchpoint: the page is protected; accesses in [lo, hi) are attributed to the host
// function (f_<guest addr>) doing them, then the page is reopened until the next re-arm.
uint64_t g_watch_lo, g_watch_hi;
static uint64_t watch_page;
static void *watch_thread(void *a) {
    (void)a;
    int r = plat_protect(watch_page, PLAT_PAGE, PLAT_PROT_NONE);
    fprintf(stderr, "[watch] page %llx protect -> %d\n", (unsigned long long)watch_page, r);
    for (;;) { plat_protect(watch_page, PLAT_PAGE, PLAT_PROT_NONE); usleep(100); }
    return NULL;
}
void watch_arm(void) {
    if (!g_watch_lo || watch_page) return;
    watch_page = g_watch_lo & ~(PLAT_PAGE - 1);
    pthread_t t;
    pthread_create(&t, NULL, watch_thread, NULL);
}

bool rt_fault_watch(uint64_t fa, uint64_t pc) {
    if (!watch_page || fa < watch_page || fa >= watch_page + PLAT_PAGE) return false;
    if (fa >= g_watch_lo && fa < g_watch_hi) {
        static char seen[64][48];
        static int nseen;
        const char *nm = host_sym(pc, NULL);
        if (!nm) nm = "?";
        char key[48];  // (each function + offset once)
        snprintf(key, sizeof key, "%.36s+%llx", nm, (unsigned long long)(fa - g_watch_lo));
        bool found = false;
        for (int i = 0; i < nseen; i++) found |= !strcmp(seen[i], key);
        if (!found && nseen < 64) {
            snprintf(seen[nseen++], 48, "%s", key);
            fprintf(stderr, "[watch] +%#llx by %s\n", fa - g_watch_lo, nm);
        }
    }
    plat_protect(watch_page, PLAT_PAGE, PLAT_PROT_RW);
    return true;
}

void rt_fault_report(const char *what, uint64_t fa, uint64_t pc, uint64_t lr) {
    uint64_t po = 0, lo = 0;
    const char *ps = host_sym(pc, &po), *ls = host_sym(lr, &lo);
    fprintf(stderr, "\n*** %s accessing %#llx\n    host pc %llx (%s+%llx)\n    host lr %llx (%s)\n", what,
            (unsigned long long)fa, (unsigned long long)pc, ps ? ps : "?", (unsigned long long)po,
            (unsigned long long)lr, ls ? ls : "?");
    rt_fatal_trace();
}

void crash_handler_install(void) { plat_crash_handler_install(); }

```

`runtime/fnhook.c`:

```c
// Guest function hooks. Every generated function starts with FN_ENTER (runtime/cpu.h); while g_fnhook is set it
// calls rt_fnhook first, and a hook that returns 1 has handled the call - the guest function returns at once (the
// hook sets x0 etc. as the function would). rt_call_original runs the game's own function from inside a hook
// (wrapping). Cost when no hook is registered: one predictable branch per call.
//
// Investigation (docs/MODO-BATALHA.md): LARECOMP_HOOK_DUMP="<addr>:<arg>,<arg>...[;<addr>:...]" logs, the first
// LARECOMP_HOOK_DUMP_MAX (default 4) times each function is entered, the registers x0..x7 and the memory the args
// name: "x2:30" = 0x30 bytes at x2, "*x0:400" = 0x400 bytes at the pointer stored at x0. LARECOMP_HOOK_DUMP_FRAMES=
// <first>-<last> limits it to those presents (the count then starts there).
#include <stdatomic.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "gamelib.h"
#include "gamesetup.h"
#include "hle.h"

volatile int g_fnhook;

typedef int (*FnHook)(Cpu *c, uint64_t addr);
#define NHOOK 1024
static struct { uint64_t addr; FnHook fn; } hooks[NHOOK];
static __thread uint64_t bypass;  // rt_call_original: the next entry of this function is the original running

// The runtime's hooks are written with addresses of Let's Go Eevee 1.0.0's main (the build the research was done on,
// docs/). The same functions in the other known builds, found by tools/addrmap.py (the code matches instruction by
// instruction, struct offsets included): each registration is kept as written and the hook table is rebuilt for the
// running build (rt_fnhook_set_build, before each boot; an unknown build gets none). Hooks at addresses the user gave
// (LARECOMP_HOOK_DUMP) are taken as they are.
static const uint64_t k_pikachu_100[][2] = {
    {0x700011ece0, 0x700011ecb0}, {0x700011ee50, 0x700011ee20}, {0x700017f0a0, 0x700017f070},
    {0x70002185d0, 0x70002185a0}, {0x70002186a0, 0x7000218670}, {0x7000289ac0, 0x7000289a90},
    {0x7000289b40, 0x7000289b10}, {0x7000289f60, 0x7000289f30}, {0x7000289fd0, 0x7000289fa0},
    {0x700028bb60, 0x700028bb30}, {0x700028ef70, 0x700028ef40}, {0x70002bad00, 0x70002bacd0},
    {0x70002f60c0, 0x70002f6090}, {0x70002f65d0, 0x70002f65a0}, {0x70002f78d0, 0x70002f78a0},
    {0x70002f8bb0, 0x70002f8b80}, {0x70003058f0, 0x70003058c0}, {0x7000305a98, 0x7000305a68},
    {0x7000305ad0, 0x7000305aa0}, {0x70006237b0, 0x7000623750}, {0x7000641190, 0x7000641130},
    {0x7000663660, 0x7000663600}, {0x7000664cd0, 0x7000664c70},
    {0x70002462e0, 0x70002462b0}, {0x7000197e90, 0x7000197e60}, {0x7000198b20, 0x7000198af0},
    {0x700021b720, 0x700021b6f0}, {0x700020b810, 0x700020b7e0},  // (fps60.c: the walking at 60 / 120 fps)
    {0x70000395f0, 0x70000395f0}, {0x7000039600, 0x7000039600}, {0x700004eb50, 0x700004eb50},  // (same place)
    {0x7000180a20, 0x70001809f0}, {0x7000180a70, 0x7000180a40},  // (cutscene.c: the natives EvCameraStart / End)
};
static int g_build = -1;  // GAME_BUILD_* (runtime/gamesetup.h); -1 before the first boot

uint64_t rt_addr(uint64_t eevee) {
    if (g_build == GAME_BUILD_EEVEE_100 || g_build < 0) return eevee;
    if (g_build == GAME_BUILD_PIKACHU_100)
        for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof k_pikachu_100 / sizeof *k_pikachu_100; i++)
            if (k_pikachu_100[i][0] == eevee) return k_pikachu_100[i][1];
    return 0;
}

#define NREG 256
static struct { uint64_t addr; FnHook fn; bool user; } regs[NREG];
static int nregs;

static void add_hook(uint64_t addr, FnHook fn) {
    if (!addr) return;
    uint32_t s = (uint32_t)((addr >> 2) * 0x9E3779B1u) & (NHOOK - 1);
    while (hooks[s].addr && hooks[s].addr != addr) s = (s + 1) & (NHOOK - 1);
    // (the function before the address: hooks are also added while the game runs - the F12 menu's frame rate - and a
    // thread looking the slot up must not find the address without its function)
    hooks[s].fn = fn;
    atomic_thread_fence(memory_order_release);
    hooks[s].addr = addr;
    g_fnhook = 1;
}

static void reg(uint64_t addr, FnHook fn, bool user) {
    for (int i = 0; i < nregs; i++)
        if (regs[i].addr == addr && regs[i].user == user) { regs[i].fn = fn; goto add; }
    if (nregs == NREG) { LOG("[fnhook] too many hooks\n"); return; }
    regs[nregs].addr = addr, regs[nregs].fn = fn, regs[nregs].user = user, nregs++;
add:
    if (user) add_hook(addr, fn);
    else if (g_build >= 0) {
        uint64_t a = rt_addr(addr);
        if (!a) LOG("[fnhook] %llx: no such function in this build\n", (unsigned long long)addr);
        add_hook(a, fn);
    }
}

void rt_register_fnhook(uint64_t addr, FnHook fn) { reg(addr, fn, false); }
// A hook at an address of the running build as it is (research: LARECOMP_STEP_SCALE, as LARECOMP_HOOK_DUMP's)
void rt_register_fnhook_raw(uint64_t addr, FnHook fn) { reg(addr, fn, true); }

void rt_fnhook_set_build(int build) {
    if (build == g_build) return;
    g_build = build;
    memset(hooks, 0, sizeof hooks);
    g_fnhook = 0;
    int n = nregs;
    nregs = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) reg(regs[i].addr, regs[i].fn, regs[i].user);
}

int rt_fnhook(Cpu *c, uint64_t addr) {
    if (bypass == addr) { bypass = 0; return 0; }
    uint32_t s = (uint32_t)((addr >> 2) * 0x9E3779B1u) & (NHOOK - 1);
    while (hooks[s].addr) {
        if (hooks[s].addr == addr) return hooks[s].fn(c, addr);
        s = (s + 1) & (NHOOK - 1);
    }
    return 0;
}

// The game's function at addr (gamelib tables), run as if called: x0.. as set by the caller of the hook.
// addr: the hooked function (as the hook received it) or an Eevee 1.0.0 address from the runtime's code (translated).
void rt_call_original(Cpu *c, uint64_t addr) {
    if (g_build == GAME_BUILD_PIKACHU_100)
        for (size_t i = 0; i < sizeof k_pikachu_100 / sizeof *k_pikachu_100; i++)
            if (k_pikachu_100[i][0] == addr) { addr = k_pikachu_100[i][1]; break; }
    const GameLibTables *t = gamelib_tables();
    for (uint32_t m = 0; t && m < t->nmods; m++) {
        const GameLibModule *md = &t->mods[m];
        uint64_t lo = 0, hi = *md->count;
        while (lo < hi) {
            uint64_t mid = (lo + hi) / 2;
            if (md->addrs[mid] < addr) lo = mid + 1;
            else hi = mid;
        }
        if (lo < *md->count && md->addrs[lo] == addr) {
            bypass = addr;
            md->fns[lo](c);
            return;
        }
    }
    LOG("[fnhook] no game function at %llx\n", (unsigned long long)addr);
}

// ---- LARECOMP_HOOK_DUMP
typedef struct { uint64_t addr; int nargs; struct { int reg, deref; uint32_t len; } arg[8]; _Atomic int hits; } Dump;
static Dump dumps[32];
static int ndumps, dump_max = 4;

static bool guest_ptr(uint64_t p) { return p >= 0x7000000000ull && p < 0x7800000000ull; }

static void hexdump(const char *what, uint64_t p, uint32_t len) {
    LOG("[hook]   %s @%llx (%u bytes):\n", what, (unsigned long long)p, len);
    if (!guest_ptr(p)) { LOG("[hook]     (not guest memory)\n"); return; }
    const uint8_t *b = (const uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)p;
    for (uint32_t o = 0; o < len; o += 16) {
        char line[128];
        int n = snprintf(line, sizeof line, "[hook]     +%03x:", o);
        for (uint32_t k = 0; k < 16 && o + k < len; k += 4) n += snprintf(line + n, sizeof line - n, " %08x", *(const uint32_t *)(b + o + k));
        LOG("%s\n", line);
    }
}

static long dump_from = -1, dump_to = -1;  // LARECOMP_HOOK_DUMP_FRAMES=<first>-<last>: only during those presents

static int dump_hook(Cpu *c, uint64_t addr) {
    extern uint64_t renderer_present_count(void);
    uint64_t frame = renderer_present_count();
    if (dump_from >= 0 && ((long)frame < dump_from || (long)frame > dump_to)) return 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < ndumps; i++) {
        Dump *d = &dumps[i];
        if (d->addr != addr || atomic_fetch_add(&d->hits, 1) >= dump_max) continue;
        LOG("[hook] f%llu %llx entered (#%d) from lr %llx: x0 %llx x1 %llx x2 %llx x3 %llx x4 %llx x5 %llx x6 %llx x7 %llx\n",
            (unsigned long long)frame, (unsigned long long)addr, d->hits, (unsigned long long)c->x[30], (unsigned long long)c->x[0], (unsigned long long)c->x[1],
            (unsigned long long)c->x[2], (unsigned long long)c->x[3], (unsigned long long)c->x[4], (unsigned long long)c->x[5],
            (unsigned long long)c->x[6], (unsigned long long)c->x[7]);
        for (int k = 0; k < d->nargs; k++) {
            uint64_t p = c->x[d->arg[k].reg];
            char what[16];
            snprintf(what, sizeof what, "%sx%d", d->arg[k].deref ? "*" : "", d->arg[k].reg);
            if (d->arg[k].deref) p = guest_ptr(p) ? *(const uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)p : 0;
            hexdump(what, p, d->arg[k].len);
        }
    }
    return 0;  // (the game's function runs as usual)
}

__attribute__((constructor)) static void hook_dump_init(void) {
    const char *e = getenv("LARECOMP_HOOK_DUMP");
    if (!e) return;
    if (getenv("LARECOMP_HOOK_DUMP_MAX")) dump_max = atoi(getenv("LARECOMP_HOOK_DUMP_MAX"));
    if (getenv("LARECOMP_HOOK_DUMP_FRAMES")) {
        const char *f = getenv("LARECOMP_HOOK_DUMP_FRAMES");
        dump_from = atol(f);
        dump_to = strchr(f, '-') ? atol(strchr(f, '-') + 1) : dump_from;
    }
    char buf[1024];
    snprintf(buf, sizeof buf, "%s", e);
    for (char *fn = strtok(buf, ";"); fn && ndumps < 32; fn = strtok(NULL, ";")) {
        Dump *d = &dumps[ndumps];
        char *colon = strchr(fn, ':');
        d->addr = strtoull(fn, NULL, 16);
        for (char *a = colon ? colon + 1 : NULL; a && *a && d->nargs < 8;) {
            int deref = *a == '*';
            if (deref) a++;
            if (*a != 'x') break;
            int reg = (int)strtol(a + 1, &a, 10);
            uint32_t len = *a == ':' ? (uint32_t)strtoul(a + 1, &a, 16) : 0x40;
            d->arg[d->nargs].reg = reg;
            d->arg[d->nargs].deref = deref;
            d->arg[d->nargs].len = len;
            d->nargs++;
            while (*a == ',') a++;
        }
        ndumps++;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < ndumps; i++) reg(dumps[i].addr, dump_hook, true);
}
```

`runtime/fnprof.c`:

```c
// Function-entry profiler. LARECOMP_FNPROF=<from>:<to> counts guest function entries (every generated
// function calls FN_ENTER) between those presented frames, then writes build/fnprof.txt (addr, count, order of
// first entry, guest lr of that first entry; most called first). Diffing two runs shows which game functions a change brings in; counts also show hot code.
#include <stdatomic.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

#include "hle.h"
#include "platform.h"

volatile int g_fnprof;

#define NSLOT (1 << 18)
static struct { _Atomic uint64_t addr; _Atomic uint64_t count; uint64_t first, lr; } slots[NSLOT];
static _Atomic uint64_t first_seq;  // order of first entry (third column), and the guest lr of that entry (fourth)

// LARECOMP_FNPROF_BT=<hex addr>[,...]: also print the host backtrace (guest functions are f_<addr>) the first time
// each listed function is entered inside the window - who calls it
// (LARECOMP_FNPROF_BT_MAX=<n>: the first n entries instead of only the first)
static uint64_t bt_addrs[256];
static int bt_n = -1, bt_max = 1;
static _Atomic uint8_t bt_done[256];

uint64_t g_bt_first_x0;

static void bt_check(uint64_t a, uint64_t lr, uint64_t x0) {
    if (bt_n < 0) {
        bt_n = 0;
        const char *e = getenv("LARECOMP_FNPROF_BT");
        if (getenv("LARECOMP_FNPROF_BT_MAX")) bt_max = atoi(getenv("LARECOMP_FNPROF_BT_MAX"));
        for (const char *p = e; p && *p && bt_n < 256;) {
            bt_addrs[bt_n++] = strtoull(p, (char **)&p, 16);
            while (*p == ',' || *p == ' ') p++;
        }
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < bt_n; i++)
        if (bt_addrs[i] == a && atomic_fetch_add(&bt_done[i], 1) < bt_max) {
            if (i == 0) g_bt_first_x0 = x0;
            uint64_t vt = x0 >= 0x7000000000ull && x0 < 0x7800000000ull ? *(uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)x0 : 0;
            uint64_t v100 = vt >= 0x7000000000ull && vt < 0x7800000000ull ? *(uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)(vt + 0x100) : 0;
            uint64_t p8 = x0 >= 0x7000000000ull && x0 < 0x7800000000ull ? *(uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)(x0 + 8) : 0;
            fprintf(stderr, "[fnprof-bt] %llx entered from guest lr %llx x0 %llx (vtable %llx, +0x100 %llx, [x0+8] %llx):\n",
                    (unsigned long long)a, (unsigned long long)lr, (unsigned long long)x0, (unsigned long long)vt,
                    (unsigned long long)v100, (unsigned long long)p8);
            plat_print_backtrace();  // (execinfo is macOS / glibc only)
        }
}

void fnprof_hit(uint64_t a, uint64_t lr, uint64_t x0) {
    if (bt_n) bt_check(a, lr, x0);
    uint32_t h = (uint32_t)((a >> 2) * 0x9E3779B1u) & (NSLOT - 1);
    for (int n = 0; n < NSLOT; n++, h = (h + 1) & (NSLOT - 1)) {
        uint64_t cur = atomic_load_explicit(&slots[h].addr, memory_order_relaxed);
        if (cur == 0 && atomic_compare_exchange_strong(&slots[h].addr, &cur, a)) {
            slots[h].first = atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&first_seq, 1, memory_order_relaxed) + 1;
            slots[h].lr = lr;
            atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&slots[h].count, 1, memory_order_relaxed);
            return;
        }
        if (cur == a) {
            atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&slots[h].count, 1, memory_order_relaxed);
            return;
        }
    }
}

static int cmp(const void *x, const void *y) {
    uint64_t a = ((const uint64_t *)x)[1], b = ((const uint64_t *)y)[1];
    return a < b ? 1 : a > b ? -1 : 0;
}

void fnprof_frame(uint64_t frame) {
    static long from = -2, to;
    if (from == -2) {
        from = -1;
        const char *e = getenv("LARECOMP_FNPROF");
        if (e && sscanf(e, "%ld:%ld", &from, &to) != 2) from = -1;
    }
    if (from < 0) return;
    if ((long)frame == from) { g_fnprof = 1; LOG("[fnprof] on at frame %llu\n", (unsigned long long)frame); }
    if ((long)frame != to) return;
    g_fnprof = 0;
    uint64_t (*rows)[4] = malloc(sizeof(uint64_t[4]) * NSLOT);
    int n = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < NSLOT; i++)
        if (slots[i].addr) { rows[n][0] = slots[i].addr; rows[n][1] = slots[i].count; rows[n][2] = slots[i].first; rows[n][3] = slots[i].lr; n++; }
    qsort(rows, n, sizeof rows[0], cmp);
    const char *out = getenv("LARECOMP_FNPROF_OUT") ? getenv("LARECOMP_FNPROF_OUT") : "build/fnprof.txt";  // (parallel runs)
    FILE *f = fopen(out, "w");
    for (int i = 0; f && i < n; i++)
        fprintf(f, "%llx %llu %llu %llx\n", (unsigned long long)rows[i][0], (unsigned long long)rows[i][1],
                (unsigned long long)rows[i][2], (unsigned long long)rows[i][3]);
    if (f) fclose(f);
    free(rows);
    LOG("[fnprof] %d functions, written %s (frames %ld-%ld)\n", n, out, from, to);
    from = -1;
}

// LARECOMP_FNPROF=0:<to>: profile from process start (threads the game starts before the first frame)
__attribute__((constructor)) static void fnprof_early(void) {
    const char *e = getenv("LARECOMP_FNPROF");
    if (e && e[0] == '0' && e[1] == ':') g_fnprof = 1;
}

```

`runtime/gamebuild.c`:

```c
// Builds the game code library on the player's machine (runtime/gamebuild.h).
#include "gamebuild.h"

#include <pthread.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/stat.h>

#include "gamelib.h"
#include "paths.h"
#include "platform.h"
#include "rt.h"

// From the Makefile: the flags the game code is compiled and linked with (as `make` builds it in a source checkout)
#ifndef GAMELIB_CFLAGS
#define GAMELIB_CFLAGS "-O1 -fno-strict-aliasing -fvisibility=hidden"
#endif
#ifndef GAMELIB_SHARED
#define GAMELIB_SHARED "-shared"
#endif

#ifdef _WIN32
#define SEP "\\"
#else
#define SEP "/"
#endif

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ child processes
// Every one running, so that quitting mid-build ends them too (atexit) instead of leaving compilers behind.
#define MAX_PROCS 80
static pthread_mutex_t g_plock = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;
static PlatProc g_procs[MAX_PROCS];
static int g_nprocs;
static bool g_quitting;

static void end_all(void) {
    pthread_mutex_lock(&g_plock);
    g_quitting = true;
    for (int i = 0; i < g_nprocs; i++) plat_proc_kill(g_procs[i]);
    g_nprocs = 0;
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_plock);
}

static PlatProc spawn(char **argv, const char *log) {
    pthread_mutex_lock(&g_plock);
    PlatProc p = g_quitting ? 0 : plat_spawn((const char *const *)argv, log, false);
    if (p && g_nprocs < MAX_PROCS) g_procs[g_nprocs++] = p;
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_plock);
    return p;
}

// plat_proc_wait without blocking, then forgotten once it has ended
static int finished(PlatProc p) {
    pthread_mutex_lock(&g_plock);
    int r = plat_proc_wait(p, false);
    if (r >= 0)
        for (int i = 0; i < g_nprocs; i++)
            if (g_procs[i] == p) { g_procs[i] = g_procs[--g_nprocs]; break; }
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_plock);
    return r;
}

static void stop(PlatProc p) {  // ends one that is still running, then forgotten
    pthread_mutex_lock(&g_plock);
    bool ours = false;
    for (int i = 0; i < g_nprocs; i++)
        if (g_procs[i] == p) { g_procs[i] = g_procs[--g_nprocs]; ours = true; break; }
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_plock);
    if (ours) plat_proc_kill(p);
}

static void sleep_ms(int ms) { plat_sleep_until_ns(plat_now_ns() + (uint64_t)ms * 1000000ull); }

static int wait_for(PlatProc p) {
    int r;
    while ((r = finished(p)) < 0) sleep_ms(20);
    return r;
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ argument lists
typedef struct { char **v; int n, cap; } Args;
static void add(Args *a, const char *s) {
    if (a->n + 2 > a->cap) {
        a->cap = a->cap ? a->cap * 2 : 32;
        a->v = (char **)realloc(a->v, sizeof *a->v * a->cap);
    }
    a->v[a->n++] = strdup(s);
    a->v[a->n] = NULL;
}
static void add_split(Args *a, const char *flags) {  // (space-separated, no quoting)
    char buf[1024];
    snprintf(buf, sizeof buf, "%s", flags);
    for (char *t = strtok(buf, " "); t; t = strtok(NULL, " ")) add(a, t);
}
static void args_free(Args *a) {
    for (int i = 0; i < a->n; i++) free(a->v[i]);
    free(a->v);
    memset(a, 0, sizeof *a);
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ the tools
typedef struct {
    char gen[1100], gen_script[1100];  // generator: lasgen, or (source checkout) the venv's python + tools/gen.py
    char cc[1100];                     // compiler: zig (as `zig cc`), or LARECOMP_CC / clang
    bool zig;
    char inc[1100], entry[1100], hle[1100];  // headers the game code includes, tools/gamelib_entry.c, HLE names
#ifdef _WIN32
    char implib[1100];  // the .exe's import library (the runtime functions the game code calls)
    char zig_rt[1100];  // the release's zig: its runtime built ahead of time (zig/rt, tools/zig_slim.sh), "" = none
#endif
} Tools;

static bool file_exists(const char *p) {
    struct stat st;
    return stat(p, &st) == 0;
}

static bool find_tools(Tools *t) {
    memset(t, 0, sizeof *t);
    const char *e = getenv("LARECOMP_GEN");
    if (e && *e) snprintf(t->gen, sizeof t->gen, "%s", e);
    else if (!rt_resource("lasgen" SEP "lasgen" PLAT_EXE_SUFFIX, NULL, t->gen, sizeof t->gen) &&
             !(rt_resource(NULL, "." PLAT_VENV_PYTHON, t->gen, sizeof t->gen) &&  // (a source checkout: .venv)
               rt_resource(NULL, "tools/gen.py", t->gen_script, sizeof t->gen_script)))
        return false;
    e = getenv("LARECOMP_CC");
    if (e && *e) snprintf(t->cc, sizeof t->cc, "%s", e);
    else if (rt_resource("zig" SEP "zig" PLAT_EXE_SUFFIX, NULL, t->cc, sizeof t->cc)) t->zig = true;
#ifndef _WIN32
    else if (rt_dev_mode() && file_exists("/usr/bin/clang")) snprintf(t->cc, sizeof t->cc, "/usr/bin/clang");
#endif
    else return false;
    if (!rt_resource("gamelib-src" SEP "cpu.h", "runtime/cpu.h", t->inc, sizeof t->inc) ||
        !rt_resource("gamelib-src" SEP "gamelib_entry.c", "tools/gamelib_entry.c", t->entry, sizeof t->entry) ||
        !rt_resource("gamelib-src" SEP "hle_symbols.txt", "runtime/hle/hle_symbols.txt", t->hle, sizeof t->hle))
        return false;
    char *s = strrchr(t->inc, '/'), *b = strrchr(t->inc, '\\');
    if (b > s) s = b;
    if (s) *s = 0;
#ifdef _WIN32
    if (!rt_resource("lasrecomp.dll.a", "build/lasrecomp.dll.a", t->implib, sizeof t->implib)) return false;
    t->zig_rt[0] = 0;
    if (t->zig && rt_resource("zig" SEP "rt" SEP "link.rsp", NULL, t->zig_rt, sizeof t->zig_rt)) {
        char *s = strrchr(t->zig_rt, '/'), *b = strrchr(t->zig_rt, '\\');
        if (b > s) s = b;
        if (s) *s = 0;
        else t->zig_rt[0] = 0;
    }
#endif
    return true;
}

bool gamebuild_available(void) {
    Tools t;
    return find_tools(&t);
}

static void compiler(Args *a, const Tools *t) {
    add(a, t->cc);
    if (t->zig) add(a, "cc");
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ generator progress (its log)
typedef struct {
    const char *name;
    char log[1100], out[1100];
    PlatProc p;
    int exit;                // -1 while running
    int files;               // chunk files written so far (complete)
    unsigned long long ci, n;  // functions written / all
} Gen;

static void read_gen_log(Gen *g) {
    FILE *f = fopen(g->log, "rb");
    if (!f) return;
    static char buf[1 << 16];
    fseek(f, 0, SEEK_END);
    long size = ftell(f);
    long from = size > (long)sizeof buf - 1 ? size - (long)sizeof buf + 1 : 0;
    fseek(f, from, SEEK_SET);
    size_t n = fread(buf, 1, sizeof buf - 1, f);
    fclose(f);
    buf[n] = 0;
    const char *last = NULL;
    for (const char *p = strstr(buf, ": progress "); p; p = strstr(p + 1, ": progress ")) last = p;
    unsigned long long ci, all;
    int files;
    if (last && sscanf(last, ": progress %llu/%llu files %d", &ci, &all, &files) == 3) {
        g->ci = ci, g->n = all;
        if (files > g->files) g->files = files;
    }
}

static void log_tail(const char *path, char *out, size_t n) {  // the last line of a log (an error message)
    out[0] = 0;
    FILE *f = fopen(path, "rb");
    if (!f) return;
    char buf[4096];
    fseek(f, 0, SEEK_END);
    long size = ftell(f);
    fseek(f, size > (long)sizeof buf - 1 ? size - (long)sizeof buf + 1 : 0, SEEK_SET);
    size_t k = fread(buf, 1, sizeof buf - 1, f);
    fclose(f);
    buf[k] = 0;
    while (k && (buf[k - 1] == '\n' || buf[k - 1] == '\r')) buf[--k] = 0;
    char *nl = strrchr(buf, '\n');
    snprintf(out, n, "%s", nl ? nl + 1 : buf);
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ compiling
typedef struct {
    char src[1100], obj[1100], log[1100];
    unsigned long long bytes;
} Unit;

typedef struct {
    Unit *u;
    int n, cap;
} Units;

static void add_unit(Units *us, const char *src, const char *work, const char *stem) {
    if (us->n == us->cap) {
        us->cap = us->cap ? us->cap * 2 : 64;
        us->u = (Unit *)realloc(us->u, sizeof *us->u * us->cap);
    }
    Unit *u = &us->u[us->n++];
    snprintf(u->src, sizeof u->src, "%s", src);
    snprintf(u->obj, sizeof u->obj, "%s" SEP "%s.o", work, stem);
    snprintf(u->log, sizeof u->log, "%s" SEP "%s.log", work, stem);
    struct stat st;
    u->bytes = stat(src, &st) == 0 ? (unsigned long long)st.st_size : 0;
}

// The flags the game code was built with (GAMELIB_CFLAGS, part of its id). zig cc reads -march=<cpu> with its own CPU
// names (x86_64_v3) and takes "-<feature>" off the end, so x86-64-v3 would be CPU "x86": the same CPU as -mcpu there.
static void add_cflags(Args *a, const Tools *t) {
    char buf[1024];
    snprintf(buf, sizeof buf, "%s", GAMELIB_CFLAGS);
    for (char *f = strtok(buf, " "); f; f = strtok(NULL, " ")) {
        if (t->zig && !strncmp(f, "-march=", 7)) {
            char cpu[128];
            snprintf(cpu, sizeof cpu, "-mcpu=%s", f + 7);
            for (char *c = cpu + 6; *c; c++) if (*c == '-') *c = '_';
            add(a, cpu);
        } else {
            add(a, f);
        }
    }
}

static PlatProc start_compile(const Tools *t, const Unit *u) {
    Args a = {0};
    compiler(&a, t);
    add_cflags(&a, t);
    char inc[1200];
    snprintf(inc, sizeof inc, "-I%s", t->inc);
    add(&a, inc);
    add(&a, "-DGAMELIB_ID=\"" GAMELIB_ID "\"");
    add(&a, "-c");
    add(&a, u->src);
    add(&a, "-o");
    add(&a, u->obj);
    PlatProc p = spawn(a.v, u->log);
    args_free(&a);
    return p;
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ the build
bool gamebuild_run(const char *game_dir, const GameBuildOpts *o, char *why, size_t why_size) {
    uint64_t t0 = plat_now_ns();
    static bool registered;
    if (!registered) registered = true, atexit(end_all);
    Tools t;
    if (!find_tools(&t)) {
        snprintf(why, why_size, "the game code builder is missing from this copy of " RT_APP_NAME);
        return false;
    }
    char work[1100], lib[1100], tmp[1100];
    snprintf(work, sizeof work, "%s" SEP ".gamebuild", game_dir);
    snprintf(lib, sizeof lib, "%s" SEP "%s", game_dir, GAMELIB_NAME);
    snprintf(tmp, sizeof tmp, "%s" SEP "%s.tmp", work, GAMELIB_NAME);
    rt_remove_game_file(game_dir, ".gamebuild");
    rt_remove_game_file(game_dir, GAMELIB_NAME);
    rt_remove_game_file(game_dir, GAMELIB_NAME ".id");
    mkdir(work, 0755);
    if (t.zig) {  // its caches in the work folder too (deleted below), not ~/.cache: hundreds of MB, used once
        char zc[1200];
        snprintf(zc, sizeof zc, "%s" SEP "zig-cache", work);
#ifdef _WIN32
        _putenv_s("ZIG_GLOBAL_CACHE_DIR", zc);
        _putenv_s("ZIG_LOCAL_CACHE_DIR", zc);
#else
        setenv("ZIG_GLOBAL_CACHE_DIR", zc, 1);
        setenv("ZIG_LOCAL_CACHE_DIR", zc, 1);
#endif
    }
    LOG("[gamebuild] generator %s%s%s, compiler %s%s, %d jobs\n", t.gen, t.gen_script[0] ? " " : "", t.gen_script,
        t.cc, t.zig ? " cc" : "", o->jobs);

    // 1. the generator, every module at once; their finished files are compiled while it goes on (bases: rt.h)
    enum { NGEN = 4 };
    Gen gens[NGEN] = {{.name = "main"}, {.name = "sdk"}, {.name = "subsdk0"}, {.name = "subsdk1"}};
    static const char *const base[NGEN] = {"0x7000000000", "0x7004000000", "0x7006000000", "0x7008000000"};
    bool ok = true;
    for (int i = 0; i < NGEN && ok; i++) {
        Gen *g = &gens[i];
        g->exit = -1;
        snprintf(g->log, sizeof g->log, "%s" SEP "gen_%s.log", work, g->name);
        snprintf(g->out, sizeof g->out, "%s" SEP "%s", work, g->name);
        char nso[1100];
        snprintf(nso, sizeof nso, "%s" SEP "exefs" SEP "%s", game_dir, g->name);
        Args a = {0};
        add(&a, t.gen);
        if (t.gen_script[0]) add(&a, t.gen_script);
        add(&a, g->name);
        add(&a, nso);
        add(&a, base[i]);
        add(&a, g->out);
        if (i == 1) { add(&a, "--hle"); add(&a, t.hle); }
        g->p = spawn(a.v, g->log);
        args_free(&a);
        if (!g->p) { snprintf(why, why_size, "the game code builder didn't start"); ok = false; }
    }

    Units units = {0};
    int queued[NGEN] = {0};  // chunk files of each module put in units so far
    bool tables[NGEN] = {false};
    int next = 0, jobs = o->jobs < 1 ? 1 : o->jobs > 64 ? 64 : o->jobs;
    struct { PlatProc p; int unit; } run[64];
    int nrun = 0;
    unsigned long long done_bytes = 0;
    double shown = 0;
    {
        add_unit(&units, t.entry, work, "gamelib_entry");
    }
    while (ok) {
        // generator progress, newly finished files
        bool gens_done = true;
        double gen_frac = 0;
        unsigned long long written = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < NGEN; i++) {
            Gen *g = &gens[i];
            if (g->exit < 0) {
                read_gen_log(g);
                int r = finished(g->p);
                if (r >= 0) {
                    g->exit = r;
                    read_gen_log(g);
                    if (r != 0) {
                        char last[300];
                        log_tail(g->log, last, sizeof last);
                        LOG("[gamebuild] generator (%s) failed: %s\n", g->name, last);
                        snprintf(why, why_size, "the game code couldn't be prepared");
                        ok = false;
                    }
                }
            }
            if (g->exit != 0) gens_done = false;
            for (; queued[i] < g->files; queued[i]++) {
                char src[1100], stem[64];
                snprintf(stem, sizeof stem, "%s_%03d", g->name, queued[i]);
                snprintf(src, sizeof src, "%s" SEP "%s.c", g->out, stem);
                add_unit(&units, src, work, stem);
            }
            if (g->exit == 0 && !tables[i]) {
                char src[1100], stem[64];
                snprintf(stem, sizeof stem, "%s_table", g->name);
                snprintf(src, sizeof src, "%s" SEP "%s.c", g->out, stem);
                add_unit(&units, src, work, stem);
                tables[i] = true;
            }
            gen_frac += (g->exit == 0 ? 1 : g->n ? (double)g->ci / (double)g->n : 0) / NGEN;  // (0..1 over all modules)
        }
        if (!ok) break;
        for (int k = 0; k < units.n; k++) written += units.u[k].bytes;

        // compiles
        while (nrun < jobs && next < units.n) {
            PlatProc p = start_compile(&t, &units.u[next]);
            if (!p) { snprintf(why, why_size, "the compiler didn't start"); ok = false; break; }
            run[nrun].p = p, run[nrun].unit = next++;
            nrun++;
        }
        for (int k = 0; k < nrun; k++) {
            int r = finished(run[k].p);
            if (r < 0) continue;
            Unit *u = &units.u[run[k].unit];
            if (r != 0) {
                char last[300];
                log_tail(u->log, last, sizeof last);
                LOG("[gamebuild] compiling %s failed: %s\n", u->src, last);
                snprintf(why, why_size, "the game code didn't compile");
                ok = false;
            }
            done_bytes += u->bytes;
            if (run[k].unit > 0) remove(u->src);  // (generated C, done with: not kept. Unit 0 is the shipped entry file)
            run[k--] = run[--nrun];
        }
        if (!ok) break;
        if (gens_done && next == units.n && nrun == 0) break;

        // progress: the generator's share (its functions written), the compiler's (bytes of C compiled, of an
        // estimate of all of it while the generator still writes)
        double est_total = gens_done ? (double)written : gen_frac > 0.02 ? (double)written / gen_frac : 0;
        double comp_frac = est_total > 0 ? (double)done_bytes / est_total : 0;
        if (comp_frac > 1) comp_frac = 1;
        double f = 0.2 * gen_frac + 0.75 * comp_frac;
        double secs = (double)(plat_now_ns() - t0) / 1e9;
        if (gen_frac == 0) f = 0.05 * (secs / (secs + 20));  // (the generator's first pass: no count yet)
        if (f > shown) shown = f;
        if (o->progress) o->progress(shown, gen_frac < 1 && !gens_done ? "Reading the game code..." : "Recompiling...");
        sleep_ms(50);
    }
    for (int k = 0; k < nrun; k++) stop(run[k].p);  // (a failure: the rest is of no use - the failure shows at once)
    for (int i = 0; i < NGEN; i++)
        if (gens[i].p && gens[i].exit < 0) stop(gens[i].p);

    // 2. link
    if (ok) {
        if (o->progress) o->progress(shown > 0.95 ? shown : 0.95, "Finishing...");
        char rsp[1100], log[1100];
        snprintf(rsp, sizeof rsp, "%s" SEP "link.rsp", work);
        snprintf(log, sizeof log, "%s" SEP "link.log", work);
        FILE *f = fopen(rsp, "wb");
        if (f) {
            for (int k = 0; k < units.n; k++) {  // (forward slashes: the response file's backslashes are escapes)
                fputc('"', f);
                for (const char *c = units.u[k].obj; *c; c++) fputc(*c == '\\' ? '/' : *c, f);
                fputs("\"\n", f);
            }
            fclose(f);
        }
        Args a = {0};
        char at[1200];
        snprintf(at, sizeof at, "@%s", rsp);
#ifdef _WIN32
        if (t.zig_rt[0]) {  // the linker itself, with the runtime built ahead of time (its flags and libraries: link.rsp)
            char opt[1200];
            add(&a, t.cc);
            add(&a, "lld-link");
            snprintf(opt, sizeof opt, "@%s" SEP "link.rsp", t.zig_rt);
            add(&a, opt);
            snprintf(opt, sizeof opt, "-LIBPATH:%s", t.zig_rt);
            add(&a, opt);
            snprintf(opt, sizeof opt, "-OUT:%s", tmp);
            add(&a, opt);
            add(&a, at);
            add(&a, t.implib);
        } else
#endif
        {
            compiler(&a, &t);
            add_split(&a, GAMELIB_SHARED);
            add(&a, "-o");
            add(&a, tmp);
            add(&a, at);
#ifdef _WIN32
            add(&a, t.implib);
#endif
        }
        PlatProc p = f ? spawn(a.v, log) : 0;
        args_free(&a);
        int r = p ? wait_for(p) : 255;
        if (r != 0) {
            char last[300];
            log_tail(log, last, sizeof last);
            LOG("[gamebuild] linking failed: %s\n", last);
            snprintf(why, why_size, "the game code didn't link");
            ok = false;
        }
    }
    if (ok) {
        remove(lib);
        char idp[1100];
        snprintf(idp, sizeof idp, "%s.id", lib);
        FILE *f = NULL;
        if (rename(tmp, lib) != 0 || !(f = fopen(idp, "wb")) || fprintf(f, "%s\n", GAMELIB_ID) < 0) {
            snprintf(why, why_size, "the game code couldn't be saved");
            ok = false;
        }
        if (f) fclose(f);
    }
    free(units.u);
    rt_remove_game_file(game_dir, ".gamebuild");  // the C, the objects, the logs
    LOG("[gamebuild] %s in %.0fs\n", ok ? "done" : "failed", (double)(plat_now_ns() - t0) / 1e9);
    if (ok && o->progress) o->progress(1, "Finishing...");
    return ok;
}
```

```h
// (tools/gen.py; shipped frozen as lasgen/) turns exefs/main and exefs/sdk into C, the bundled compiler (zig/) builds
```
