`runtime/hle/font_hires.c`:

```c
// Sharper in-game text: the game's glyph cache drawn again at K x the resolution on the host.
//
// The game's text goes through nn::font's scalable font (in main, no symbols): TextureCache::UpdateTextureCache
// (Pikachu 1.0.0 f_70004654d0) rasterizes each new glyph with the SDK's nn::fontll engine at the glyph's font size
// and copies it into its cache texture - an 8-bit linear texture whose rows are stored bottom-up - at a cell of a
// line it allocated (one column of zeros on each side). Outline fonts get the outline glyph there and then the fill
// glyph subtracted at half strength (one channel: outline 255, fill ~128). Text is drawn from that texture with
// normalized coordinates, so an image K times as large in each axis drops in unchanged (runtime/nvn/vulkan/textures.c
// font_k): this file keeps that K x image in host memory, rasterizing every glyph the game caches a second time,
// at K x its font size, with the same engine and the same composition, into the K x cell.
//
// Where: the game's ReleasesGlyph call right after a glyph was written (recognised by the instructions around the
// return address, so it works in every build), with the cache in x19, the glyph's node in x26, the texture data in
// x23 and the outline glyph's top bearing on the caller's stack (+0x30). Node: +0x30 code, +0x34 font index, +0x36
// font size, +0x3a line kind, +0x40 / +0x42 cell x / line y, +0x44 width. Cache: +8 the engine, +0x28 / +0x2c the
// texture's size, +0x1be8 line kind -> line height, +0x1bf0 per font {+8 ascent / size}, +0x1c00 per font: outline.
// Glyph maps (nn::fontll, iType's FS_GLYPHMAP): +0xc left bearing, +0xe top bearing, +0x1c width (= bytes per row),
// +0x1e rows, +0x28 the 8-bit pixels.
//
// Always on: K from the window's height at the first glyph (one step per 720 lines, up to 4; 720p and below: off).
// LARECOMP_FONT_SCALE=<1..4> forces K (1: off, for comparisons); LARECOMP_FONT_LOG=1 logs the glyphs drawn (the
// first few hundred).
#include <math.h>
#include <pthread.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "../hle.h"

uint64_t loader_find_symbol(const char *name);
int renderer_font_scale(void);  // textures.c: K from the window

#define SYM_SET_SCALE "_ZN2nn6fontll18ScalableFontEngine8SetScaleEiiii"
#define SYM_ACQUIRE "_ZN2nn6fontll18ScalableFontEngine15AcquireGlyphmapEjt"
#define SYM_RELEASE "_ZN2nn6fontll18ScalableFontEngine13ReleasesGlyphEPv"
#define SYM_FLAGS "_ZN2nn6fontll18ScalableFontEngine8SetFlagsENS1_5FlagsE"
#define SYM_OUTLINE "_ZN2nn6fontll18ScalableFontEngine15SetOutlineWidthEt"

static uint64_t orig(const char *name, uint64_t *cache) {
    if (!*cache) *cache = loader_find_symbol(name);
    if (!*cache) FATAL("font: no SDK implementation of %s\n", name);
    return *cache;
}

// The SDK's own function, from inside a wrapper (x30 kept: the wrapper returns to the game).
static void call_sdk(Cpu *c, const char *sym, uint64_t *cache) {
    uint64_t lr = c->x[30];
    guest_call(c, orig(sym, cache));
    c->x[30] = lr;
}
static uint64_t a_scale, a_acquire, a_release, a_flags, a_outline;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- engine state the game set (restored after ours)
#define NENG 8
static struct { uint64_t eng; uint32_t flags; uint32_t outline; } g_eng[NENG];
static pthread_mutex_t g_eng_lock = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;
static int eng_slot(uint64_t e) {
    for (int i = 0; i < NENG; i++) if (g_eng[i].eng == e) return i;
    for (int i = 0; i < NENG; i++) if (!g_eng[i].eng) { g_eng[i].eng = e; g_eng[i].flags = ~0u; g_eng[i].outline = ~0u; return i; }
    return -1;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the K x images (one per glyph cache texture)
#define NCACHE 4
typedef struct {
    uint64_t addr;           // the game's texture data (texture address)
    uint32_t w, h, k;        // its size, the scale
    uint8_t *px;             // (w*k) x (h*k), rows bottom-up as the game's
    uint32_t x0, y0, x1, y1; // changed since the last upload (x1 <= x0: nothing)
} FontCache;
static FontCache g_fc[NCACHE];
static pthread_mutex_t g_fc_lock = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;

RT_ON_RESET(font_hires_reset) {
    pthread_mutex_lock(&g_fc_lock);
    for (int i = 0; i < NCACHE; i++) free(g_fc[i].px);
    memset(g_fc, 0, sizeof g_fc);
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_fc_lock);
    pthread_mutex_lock(&g_eng_lock);
    memset(g_eng, 0, sizeof g_eng);
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_eng_lock);
}

static int log_left(void) {
    static int n = -1;
    if (n < 0) n = ENV("LARECOMP_FONT_LOG") ? 400 : 0;
    return n > 0 ? n-- : 0;
}

// The K for this game (fixed at the first glyph: the cache textures keep their size).
static int font_k(void) {
    static int k;
    if (!k) {
        const char *e = ENV("LARECOMP_FONT_SCALE");
        k = e ? atoi(e) : renderer_font_scale();
        if (k < 1) k = 1;
        if (k > 4) k = 4;
        LOG("[font] glyph cache at %dx\n", k);
    }
    return k;
}

static FontCache *cache_for(uint64_t addr, uint32_t w, uint32_t h, int k) {
    for (int i = 0; i < NCACHE; i++)
        if (g_fc[i].addr == addr) return g_fc[i].w == w && g_fc[i].h == h ? &g_fc[i] : NULL;
    for (int i = 0; i < NCACHE; i++)
        if (!g_fc[i].addr) {
            uint8_t *px = calloc((size_t)w * k * h * k, 1);
            if (!px) return NULL;
            g_fc[i] = (FontCache){addr, w, h, (uint32_t)k, px, 0, 0, w * k, h * k};
            LOG("[font] glyph cache texture %llx %ux%u -> %ux%u\n", (unsigned long long)addr, w, h, w * k, h * k);
            return &g_fc[i];
        }
    return NULL;
}

// For the renderer: K if the texture at addr (w x h) is a glyph cache drawn at K x, else 1.
int font_hires_scale(uint64_t addr, uint32_t w, uint32_t h) {
    int k = 1;
    pthread_mutex_lock(&g_fc_lock);
    for (int i = 0; i < NCACHE; i++)
        if (g_fc[i].addr == addr && g_fc[i].w == w && g_fc[i].h == h) k = (int)g_fc[i].k;
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_fc_lock);
    return k;
}

// The changed part of the K x image of that texture: true (and locked until font_hires_end) with *px, the image's
// row length and the rectangle (rows counted as stored); false: not a glyph cache.
bool font_hires_begin(uint64_t addr, const uint8_t **px, uint32_t *row, uint32_t *x0, uint32_t *y0, uint32_t *x1,
                      uint32_t *y1) {
    pthread_mutex_lock(&g_fc_lock);
    for (int i = 0; i < NCACHE; i++)
        if (g_fc[i].addr == addr) {
            FontCache *f = &g_fc[i];
            *px = f->px; *row = f->w * f->k;
            *x0 = f->x0; *y0 = f->y0; *x1 = f->x1; *y1 = f->y1;
            f->x0 = f->y0 = f->x1 = f->y1 = 0;
            return true;
        }
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_fc_lock);
    return false;
}
void font_hires_end(void) { pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_fc_lock); }

static void mark(FontCache *f, uint32_t x0, uint32_t y0, uint32_t x1, uint32_t y1) {
    if (f->x1 <= f->x0) { f->x0 = x0; f->y0 = y0; f->x1 = x1; f->y1 = y1; return; }
    if (x0 < f->x0) f->x0 = x0;
    if (y0 < f->y0) f->y0 = y0;
    if (x1 > f->x1) f->x1 = x1;
    if (y1 > f->y1) f->y1 = y1;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- where the game is
static bool words_at(uint64_t lr, int from, const uint32_t *w, const uint32_t *mask, int n) {
    if (lr < MAIN_BASE + 64 || lr >= SDK_BASE) return false;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++)
        if ((((const u32u *)(uintptr_t)(lr + (int64_t)(from + i) * 4))[0] & mask[i]) != w[i]) return false;
    return true;
}
#define BL 0x94000000u, 0xFC000000u
// ReleasesGlyph right after a glyph went into the cache (UpdateTextureCache, Pikachu 1.0.0 +0x7dc):
//   ldr x0, [x19, #0x1e80] / bl (unmap) / ldr x0, [x19, #8] / mov x1, x20 / bl ReleasesGlyph / ldr x0, [x19, #8] / bl / mov w23, #0x1c
static bool site_written(uint64_t lr) {
    static const uint32_t w[] = {0xf94f4260, 0x94000000, 0xf9400660, 0xaa1403e1, 0x94000000, 0xf9400660, 0x94000000, 0x321e0bf7};
    static const uint32_t m[] = {~0u, 0xFC000000u, ~0u, ~0u, 0xFC000000u, ~0u, 0xFC000000u, ~0u};
    static uint64_t yes, no;
    if (lr == yes) return true;
    if (lr == no) return false;
    bool r = words_at(lr, -5, w, m, 8);
    if (r) yes = lr; else no = lr;
    return r;
}
// AcquireGlyphmap of a glyph's first (or only) map: fcvtzs w27, s0 / bl / mov x20, x0 / ldr x0, [x19, #8] / bl / ldrh w9, [x20, #0x1e]
static bool site_first_map(uint64_t lr) {
    static const uint32_t w[] = {0x1e38001b, 0x94000000, 0xaa0003f4, 0xf9400660, 0x94000000, 0x79403e89};
    static const uint32_t m[] = {~0u, 0xFC000000u, ~0u, ~0u, 0xFC000000u, ~0u};
    static uint64_t yes, no;
    if (lr == yes) return true;
    if (lr == no) return false;
    bool r = words_at(lr, -2, w, m, 6);
    if (r) yes = lr; else no = lr;
    return r;
}

// The glyph's first map as the game got it (an outline font's outline glyph is released before the cell is done).
static __thread struct { uint64_t node; int16_t lo_x, hi_y; uint16_t w, rows; } t_first;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the engine, called from here
static uint64_t sdk(Cpu *c, const char *sym, uint64_t *cache, uint64_t a0, uint64_t a1, uint64_t a2, uint64_t a3, uint64_t a4) {
    c->x[0] = a0; c->x[1] = a1; c->x[2] = a2; c->x[3] = a3; c->x[4] = a4;
    call_sdk(c, sym, cache);
    return c->x[0];
}

typedef struct { int16_t lo_x, hi_y; int w, rows; } MapInfo;
static MapInfo map_info(uint64_t g) {
    return (MapInfo){*(int16_t *)(uintptr_t)(g + 0xc), *(int16_t *)(uintptr_t)(g + 0xe), *(int16_t *)(uintptr_t)(g + 0x1c),
                     *(int16_t *)(uintptr_t)(g + 0x1e)};
}

// The glyph of that node again at K x into the K x image.
static void draw_hires(Cpu *c, uint64_t cache, uint64_t node, uint64_t tex, int k) {
    uint64_t eng = *(u64u *)(uintptr_t)(cache + 8);
    uint32_t W = *(u32u *)(uintptr_t)(cache + 0x28), H = *(u32u *)(uintptr_t)(cache + 0x2c);
    uint32_t code = *(u32u *)(uintptr_t)(node + 0x30);
    uint16_t fi = *(u16u *)(uintptr_t)(node + 0x34), size = *(u16u *)(uintptr_t)(node + 0x36);
    uint8_t kind = *(u8a *)(uintptr_t)(node + 0x3a);
    uint32_t cx = *(u16u *)(uintptr_t)(node + 0x40), ly = *(u16u *)(uintptr_t)(node + 0x42), cw = *(u16u *)(uintptr_t)(node + 0x44);
    uint64_t tbl = *(u64u *)(uintptr_t)(cache + 0x1bf0) + (uint64_t)fi * 0x1c;
    int asc = (int)(*(float *)(uintptr_t)(tbl + 8) * (float)size + 0.5f);
    bool outline = *(u8a *)(uintptr_t)(*(u64u *)(uintptr_t)(cache + 0x1c00) + fi) != 0;
    if (!W || !H || W > 8192 || H > 8192 || !size || t_first.node != node) return;
    // line height (the game's own function: cells reach that far down)
    c->x[0] = kind;
    {
        uint64_t lr = c->x[30];
        guest_call(c, *(u64u *)(uintptr_t)(cache + 0x1be8));
        c->x[30] = lr;
    }
    uint32_t lh = (uint32_t)c->x[0] & 0xffff;
    if (!lh || ly + lh > H) lh = H - ly;

    pthread_mutex_lock(&g_eng_lock);
    int es = eng_slot(eng);
    uint32_t flags = es >= 0 ? g_eng[es].flags : ~0u, ow = es >= 0 ? g_eng[es].outline : ~0u;
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_eng_lock);

    // the K x cell: the low one's columns cx..cx+cw+1 (glyph from cx+1), rows ly..ly+lh (top-down) - all of them, its
    // empty edge columns too: left as they were, a glyph that had used them before showed as thin vertical lines
    uint32_t KW = W * k, KH = H * k;
    int cl = (int)(cx * k), cr = (int)((cx + cw + 2) * k), ct = (int)(ly * k), cb = (int)((ly + lh) * k);
    if (cr > (int)KW) cr = (int)KW;
    if (cb > (int)KH) cb = (int)KH;
    int pen_x = (int)cx + 1 - t_first.lo_x, base_y = (int)ly + asc;  // the low glyph's pen origin, baseline (top-down)

    uint8_t *cell = calloc((size_t)(cr - cl > 0 ? cr - cl : 1) * (cb - ct > 0 ? cb - ct : 1), 1);
    if (!cell) return;
    int cellw = cr - cl;
    sdk(c, SYM_SET_SCALE, &a_scale, eng, (uint64_t)(size * k) << 16, 0, 0, (uint64_t)(size * k) << 16);
    if (outline && ow != ~0u) sdk(c, SYM_OUTLINE, &a_outline, eng, ow * k, 0, 0, 0);
    uint64_t g = sdk(c, SYM_ACQUIRE, &a_acquire, eng, code, 8, 0, 0);
    int ox = 0, oy = 0;  // where the first map's top-left lands in the cell
    bool ok = g != 0;
    if (ok) {
        MapInfo m = map_info(g);
        ox = pen_x * k + m.lo_x - cl;
        oy = base_y * k - m.hi_y - ct;
        const uint8_t *bits = (const uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)(g + 0x28);
        for (int i = 0; i < m.rows; i++) {
            int y = oy + i;
            if (y < 0 || y >= cb - ct) continue;
            for (int j = 0; j < m.w; j++) {
                int x = ox + j;
                if (x >= 0 && x < cellw) cell[(size_t)y * cellw + x] = bits[(size_t)i * m.w + j];
            }
        }
        if (log_left())
            LOG("[font] U+%04x size %u (x%d) font %u%s: low %dx%d lo_x %d hi_y %d at %u,%u (line %u, asc %d) | high %dx%d lo_x %d hi_y %d\n",
                code, size, k, fi, outline ? " outline" : "", cw, t_first.rows, t_first.lo_x, t_first.hi_y, cx, ly, lh, asc,
                m.w, m.rows, m.lo_x, m.hi_y);
        sdk(c, SYM_RELEASE, &a_release, eng, g, 0, 0, 0);
    }
    if (ok && outline) {  // the fill, subtracted at half strength where the outline glyph is (as the game does)
        sdk(c, SYM_FLAGS, &a_flags, eng, 1, 0, 0, 0);
        uint64_t f = sdk(c, SYM_ACQUIRE, &a_acquire, eng, code, 8, 0, 0);
        if (f) {
            MapInfo m = map_info(f);
            const uint8_t *bits = (const uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)(f + 0x28);
            for (int i = 0; i < m.rows; i++) {
                int y = oy + i;
                if (y < 0 || y >= cb - ct) continue;
                for (int j = 0; j < m.w; j++) {
                    int x = ox + j;
                    if (x >= 0 && x < cellw) cell[(size_t)y * cellw + x] -= bits[(size_t)i * m.w + j] >> 1;
                }
            }
            sdk(c, SYM_RELEASE, &a_release, eng, f, 0, 0, 0);
        }
        sdk(c, SYM_FLAGS, &a_flags, eng, flags != ~0u ? flags : 2, 0, 0, 0);
    }
    // the game's state back
    if (outline && ow != ~0u) sdk(c, SYM_OUTLINE, &a_outline, eng, ow, 0, 0, 0);
    sdk(c, SYM_SET_SCALE, &a_scale, eng, (uint64_t)size << 16, 0, 0, (uint64_t)size << 16);

    if (ok && cellw > 0 && cb > ct) {
        pthread_mutex_lock(&g_fc_lock);
        FontCache *fc = cache_for(tex, W, H, k);
        if (fc && fc->k == (uint32_t)k)
            for (int y = ct; y < cb; y++)  // (stored bottom-up)
                memcpy(fc->px + (size_t)(KH - 1 - y) * KW + cl, cell + (size_t)(y - ct) * cellw, (size_t)cellw);
        if (fc) mark(fc, (uint32_t)cl, KH - (uint32_t)cb, (uint32_t)cr, KH - (uint32_t)ct);
        pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_fc_lock);
    }
    free(cell);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the wrappers
HLE_FUNC(SYM_SET_SCALE, font_set_scale) { call_sdk(c, SYM_SET_SCALE, &a_scale); }

HLE_FUNC(SYM_FLAGS, font_set_flags) {
    pthread_mutex_lock(&g_eng_lock);
    int s = eng_slot(c->x[0]);
    if (s >= 0) g_eng[s].flags = (uint32_t)c->x[1];
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_eng_lock);
    call_sdk(c, SYM_FLAGS, &a_flags);
}

HLE_FUNC(SYM_OUTLINE, font_set_outline) {
    pthread_mutex_lock(&g_eng_lock);
    int s = eng_slot(c->x[0]);
    if (s >= 0) g_eng[s].outline = (uint32_t)c->x[1] & 0xffff;
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_eng_lock);
    call_sdk(c, SYM_OUTLINE, &a_outline);
}

HLE_FUNC(SYM_ACQUIRE, font_acquire) {
    uint64_t lr = c->x[30], node = c->x[26];
    call_sdk(c, SYM_ACQUIRE, &a_acquire);
    if (c->x[0] && site_first_map(lr)) {
        MapInfo m = map_info(c->x[0]);
        t_first.node = node; t_first.lo_x = m.lo_x; t_first.hi_y = m.hi_y; t_first.w = (uint16_t)m.w; t_first.rows = (uint16_t)m.rows;
    }
}

HLE_FUNC(SYM_RELEASE, font_release) {
    uint64_t lr = c->x[30];
    bool written = site_written(lr);
    uint64_t cache = c->x[19], node = c->x[26], tex = c->x[23];
    call_sdk(c, SYM_RELEASE, &a_release);
    if (!written) return;
    int k = font_k();
    if (k < 2) return;
    uint64_t keep[2] = {c->x[0], c->x[1]};
    draw_hires(c, cache, node, tex, k);
    c->x[0] = keep[0]; c->x[1] = keep[1];
    t_first.node = 0;
}

```

`runtime/hle/fps60.c`:

```c
// 60 fps (experimental): the world and the menus at 60, battles and captures as the game made them (30). 120 (more
// experimental): the world at 120 the same way (G[1] = 8.33 ms), menus still 30 with the in-between image (60).
// The F12 menu switches the rate while the game runs (fps60_present, on the game thread: hooks added then).
//
// The game keeps a table of frame durations G (main+0xf7eeb8: 16.67 ms, 33.33 ms, 50 ms, ...; read through the pointer
// at main+0x15fb438). The world's update step comes from G[1] through the accessor f_7000039600; menus, battles and
// captures count their own frames, so at 60 fps they run twice as fast (docs/PESQUISA-60FPS.md). A community "60 FPS"
// patch changes G[1] for every reader; here:
//  - the animation systems take "elapsed time" as a fixed 33.33 ms per update and divide it by G[1] to get frames: the
//    time the accessor hands out is that elapsed time, so with 16.67 ms there they advance half a frame per update at
//    60 fps - right, by time (menus, the world's animations);
//  - battles and captures also count integer frames of their own: they keep the game's 33.33 ms and 30 fps (the entry
//    points of both scenes, mapped in docs/MODO-BATALHA.md, switch to it until the world's update runs again).
// Scenes move from the 30 fps side to the 60 fps side one at a time, once their frame counters are fixed.
//
// LARECOMP_FPS60=1 turns it on (settings: fps = 60). LARECOMP_G1_READERS="<addr>[,<addr>...]" (research): G[1] is
// 16.67 ms only while those functions run, to find which readers a speed comes from.
#include <stdatomic.h>
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <math.h>
#include <pthread.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "../hle.h"
#include "../settings.h"

void rt_register_fnhook(uint64_t addr, int (*fn)(Cpu *c, uint64_t addr));  // runtime/fnhook.c
void rt_call_original(Cpu *c, uint64_t addr);
uint64_t renderer_game_frame(void);

#define G1_ADDR 0x7000f7eec0ull  // G[1]: 33333334 ns
#define G1_ORIGINAL 33333334u
#define G1_60HZ 16666667u
static uint32_t g_g1 = G1_60HZ;  // the world's step: 16.67 ms (60 fps) or 8.33 ms (120)
static int g_rate = 60;
#define FIELD_UPDATE 0x70002f8bb0ull  // the world's update, every frame while it runs
#define G_ACCESSOR 0x7000039600ull    // G[index]: the world's step comes through here

static bool g_on;
static bool g_world = true;             // 60 fps now (not inside a battle or a capture)
static bool g_all60;                    // LARECOMP_FPS60=2
static bool g_special;                  // a battle or a capture started and the world hasn't updated since
#define ENCOUNTER_SCENE 0x700028ef70ull  // creates the capture scene (x0 = the encounter object)
#define BATTLE_START 0x700028bb60ull     // copies the battle's configuration

static long g_scene_start = -1;  // research: the present a capture began in (LARECOMP_SHOT_REL)
long fps60_scene_start(void) { return g_scene_start; }
static int scene_start_hook(Cpu *c, uint64_t addr) {
    if (g_scene_start < 0) {
        g_scene_start = (long)renderer_game_frame();
        LOG("[fps60] scene start %ld (f_%llx)\n", g_scene_start, (unsigned long long)addr);
    }
    (void)c, (void)addr;
    return 0;
}

static bool g_scene;  // inside a battle or a capture (until the world updates again)

// The frame counters a scene's timeline runs on (tools/patches.py) step on every other update at 60 fps: 1 = step now.
// Research (LARECOMP_FPS60_STATS=1): once a second, what the game did: presents, world updates (FIELD_UPDATE), reads of G through
// the accessor, and how many times the scene counters (tools/patches.py) were offered a step / allowed to take it.
static bool g_stats;
static unsigned long g_n_world, g_n_acc, g_n_tick_ask, g_n_tick_do;
int rt_scene_tick(void) {
    int r = !(g_all60 && g_scene && (renderer_game_frame() & 1));
    g_n_tick_ask++, g_n_tick_do += r;
    return r;
}

// Every battle / capture and the world's return after it, in the log ("[scene]"; tools/capture_loop.py reads them) and for
// the scripted input (LARECOMP_INPUT_LOOP holds still for a while after the world comes back: input.c)
static bool g_mark_scene;
static long g_world_back = -1;
long fps60_world_back(void) { return g_world_back; } bool fps60_in_scene(void) { return g_mark_scene; }
static int scene_hook(Cpu *c, uint64_t addr) {
    scene_start_hook(c, addr);  // (one hook per address: this one also marks the start for LARECOMP_SHOT_REL)
    if (!g_mark_scene) { g_mark_scene = true; LOG("[scene] start %llu (f_%llx)\n", (unsigned long long)renderer_game_frame(), (unsigned long long)addr); }
    g_scene = true;
    if (g_all60) return 0;  // LARECOMP_FPS60=2: battles and captures at 60 too (their counters halved)
    g_special = true;
    (void)c, (void)addr;
    return 0;
}

// A battle the game starts without BATTLE_START: the wild battles mode builds it through the static battles' process
// (runtime/hle/wildbattle.c), which never calls it. Without this it counted as a menu and got in-between images.
void fps60_scene_begin(void) {
    g_scene = true;
    if (!g_all60) g_special = true;
}

static bool g_field_ran;  // the world's update ran since the last present
static bool g_played;     // the world has updated at least once (before: the controller screen, the title, loading)
static int field_hook(Cpu *c, uint64_t addr) {
    g_n_world++;
    if (g_mark_scene) { g_mark_scene = false; g_world_back = (long)renderer_game_frame(); LOG("[scene] world again %ld\n", g_world_back); }
    g_field_ran = true;
    if (!g_played) LOG("[scene] the world's first update at present %llu (the title screen is over)\n", (unsigned long long)renderer_game_frame());
    g_played = true;
    g_special = false;
    g_scene = false;
    (void)c, (void)addr;
    return 0;  // (the game's function runs as usual)
}

// The frame-step timers (the accessor's x0): entries of 16 bytes, step i at +0x10 + 16 i (setter f_7000039620)
static uint64_t g_timers;
uint64_t fps60_timers(void) { return g_timers; }  // (runtime/hle/fps60_research.c)

// G[1] at 60 Hz for the duration of f: the world's step; any other scene keeps the game's value.
static int accessor_hook(Cpu *c, uint64_t addr) {
    volatile uint32_t *g1 = (volatile uint32_t *)(uintptr_t)G1_ADDR;
    g_n_acc++;
    g_timers = c->x[0];
    if (!g_on || !g_world) return 0;
    *g1 = g_g1;
    rt_call_original(c, addr);
    *g1 = G1_ORIGINAL;
    return 1;
}

static int g1_reader_hook(Cpu *c, uint64_t addr) {
    volatile uint32_t *g1 = (volatile uint32_t *)(uintptr_t)G1_ADDR;
    *g1 = G1_60HZ;
    rt_call_original(c, addr);
    *g1 = G1_ORIGINAL;
    return 1;
}

// Research (LARECOMP_FPS60_LOG=1): the frame-rate setting object the animation systems index G with (main+0x15fab08
// holds a pointer to a pointer to it; +0x88 is the index), once a second.
static void log_index(void) {
    static uint64_t last;
    uint64_t f = renderer_game_frame();
    if (f - last < 60) return;
    last = f;
    const uint64_t *slot = (const uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)(0x7000000000ull + 0x15fab08);
    const uint64_t *obj = (const uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)*slot;
    if (!obj || (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)obj < 0x7000000000ull) return;
    const uint64_t *real = (const uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)*obj;
    if (!real || (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)real < 0x7000000000ull) return;
    LOG("[fps60] present %llu: frame-rate index %d (G[idx] = %u)\n", (unsigned long long)f, *(const int32_t *)((const uint8_t *)real + 0x88),
        *(const uint32_t *)(uintptr_t)(0x7000f7eeb8ull + 8ull * (uint32_t)*(const int32_t *)((const uint8_t *)real + 0x88)));
}

bool fps60_enabled(void) { return g_on; }
int fps60_rate(void) { return g_rate; }  // the world's frame rate while on: 60 or 120
// The duration of a frame now (runtime/nvn/objects.c pacing, output_scale.c dynamic resolution): the world's at its
// rate, the rest at the game's 30
uint64_t fps60_period_ns(void) { return g_on && g_world ? 1000000000ull / (uint64_t)g_rate : 33333333ull; }
bool fps60_world(void) { return g_world; }
// A menu (the Pokédex, the bag...): the world stopped and no battle or capture runs. Logic at 30, shown at 60 with the
// in-between image (runtime/nvn/vulkan/exec.c); battles and captures get none (tried, left out: docs/HISTORICO.md 46).
bool fps60_menu(void) { return g_on && g_played && !g_world && !g_special; }
// Before the world's first update this boot: the logos, the title screen (the logo with Pikachu or Eevee), loading
// (runtime/nvn/vulkan/exec.c: SSAO at half its intensity, as in cutscenes)
bool game_title(void) { return !g_played; }

// At each present (before its pacing): was this a world frame?
void fps60_probe_present(void);
int rt_present_interval(void);
// ---- the player's walking at 60 / 120 fps
// The player moves by the walking animation's root motion (time-based: right at any rate) plus, once per world update,
// an offset of its own (MOVE_FN: position += facing x a vector x one of the movement component's parameters +0x70 /
// +0x74 / +0x78, by the stick's state - -2 cm at a run, sized for a 33.3 ms update). Per update, not per second: at 30
// fps it takes 60 cm/s off the animation's 450.8 (391 cm/s), at 60 fps 120 (331), at 120 fps 240 (211) - the player
// walked at 85 % and 53 % of the speed (measured with tools/walk_speed.sh; found with LARECOMP_WATCH_LIKE / memwatch.c:
// the writes to the player's position, in order). The same function turns the player toward the stick with a slerp
// (SLERP_FN) of t = 0.5 per update: twice / four times as fast at 60 / 120. While it runs in the world at 60 / 120 fps,
// the parameters are scaled by the step's share of 33.3 ms and the slerp's t becomes 1 - (1 - t)^share: per second,
// what the game does at 30. Eevee 1.0.0's addresses (Pikachu's: runtime/fnhook.c, tools/addrmap.py).
#define MOVE_FN 0x700021b720ull
#define SLERP_FN 0x700020b810ull
static __thread bool t_in_move;
static __thread float t_move_k;
static int move_hook(Cpu *c, uint64_t addr) {
    float k = g_on && g_world ? (float)g_g1 / (float)G1_ORIGINAL : 1.0f;
    if (k >= 0.999f || c->x[0] < 0x7000000000ull) return 0;  // (the game's own step: as it is)
    float *p = (float *)(uintptr_t)(c->x[0] + 0x70), was[3] = {p[0], p[1], p[2]};
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) p[i] = was[i] * k;
    t_in_move = true, t_move_k = k;
    rt_call_original(c, addr);
    t_in_move = false;
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) p[i] = was[i];
    return 1;
}
static int slerp_hook(Cpu *c, uint64_t addr) {
    (void)addr;
    if (!t_in_move) return 0;
    float t;
    memcpy(&t, &c->v[0], 4);
    if (t > 0 && t < 1) {
        t = 1.0f - powf(1.0f - t, t_move_k);
        memcpy(&c->v[0], &t, 4);
    }
    return 0;  // (the slerp runs with that t)
}
static bool hooked;
static void hook_all(void) {
    if (hooked) return;
    hooked = true;
    rt_register_fnhook(FIELD_UPDATE, field_hook);
    rt_register_fnhook(ENCOUNTER_SCENE, scene_hook);
    rt_register_fnhook(BATTLE_START, scene_hook);
    rt_register_fnhook(G_ACCESSOR, accessor_hook);
    if (!getenv("LARECOMP_FPS60_NOWALKFIX")) {
        extern uint64_t rt_addr(uint64_t eevee);
        rt_register_fnhook(MOVE_FN, move_hook), rt_register_fnhook(SLERP_FN, slerp_hook);
        LOG("[fps60] walking fix: movement f_%llx, turning f_%llx\n", (unsigned long long)rt_addr(MOVE_FN), (unsigned long long)rt_addr(SLERP_FN));
    }
}

// The F12 menu's frame rate (g_settings.fps), followed at each present (LARECOMP_FPS60 overrides it)
static void follow_setting(void) {
    if (getenv("LARECOMP_FPS60")) return;
    extern uint64_t rt_addr(uint64_t eevee);
    bool on = g_settings.fps >= 60 && rt_addr(FIELD_UPDATE);
    int rate = g_settings.fps == 120 ? 120 : 60;
    if (on == g_on && rate == g_rate) return;
    if (on) hook_all();
    if (on && !g_on) g_world = true, g_special = g_scene = false;  // (g_played: kept - the world has run already or not)
    g_on = on, g_rate = rate, g_g1 = (uint32_t)(1000000000u / (uint32_t)rate);
    LOG("[fps60] %s (from present %llu)\n", on ? (rate == 120 ? "120 fps" : "60 fps") : "off: 30 fps",
        (unsigned long long)renderer_game_frame());
}

void fps60_present(void) {
#ifdef _WIN32
    { extern void memwatch_present(void); memwatch_present(); }  // (research: LARECOMP_WATCH_LIKE)
#endif
    follow_setting();
    fps60_probe_present();
    if (g_stats) {
        static uint64_t t0, p0;
        extern uint64_t plat_now_ns(void);
        uint64_t now = plat_now_ns(), p = renderer_game_frame();
        if (!t0) t0 = now, p0 = p;
        if (now - t0 >= 1000000000ull) {
            LOG("[stats] t+%.2fs presents %llu world %lu acc %lu tick_ask %lu tick_do %lu scene %d interval %d G1 %u\n", (now - t0) / 1e9,
                (unsigned long long)(p - p0), g_n_world, g_n_acc, g_n_tick_ask, g_n_tick_do, g_scene, rt_present_interval(), *(volatile uint32_t *)(uintptr_t)G1_ADDR);
            t0 = now, p0 = p, g_n_world = g_n_acc = g_n_tick_ask = g_n_tick_do = 0;
        }
    }
    if (getenv("LARECOMP_FPS60_LOG")) log_index();
    if (!g_on) return;
    // 60 only while the world itself updates: menus, the Pokédex and other screens that stop it count their own frames
    // and ran twice as fast (measured: the menu opened in 4 game frames instead of 8)
    static int menu_native = -1;  // (research, LARECOMP_FPS60_MENU_NATIVE=1: menus at 60 natively, as before HISTORICO 47)
    if (menu_native < 0) menu_native = getenv("LARECOMP_FPS60_MENU_NATIVE") != NULL;
    bool w = !g_special && (g_field_ran || menu_native);
    g_field_ran = false;
    g_world = w;
    static int last = -1;  // 0 world, 1 menu (in-between images), 2 battle / capture
    int state = w ? 0 : fps60_menu() ? 1 : 2;
    static const char *const name[] = {"world: %d fps", "menu: 30 fps with in-between images", "battle / capture: 30 fps"};
    if (state != last) {
        char what[64];
        snprintf(what, sizeof what, name[state], g_rate);
        LOG("[fps60] %s from present %llu\n", what, (unsigned long long)renderer_game_frame());
    }
    last = state;
}

// Before each boot (runtime/main.c): the launcher's "60 fps (experimental)" (larecomp.ini fps = 60) turns the mode on
// when LARECOMP_FPS60 doesn't say otherwise.
void fps60_configure(void) {
    extern void settings_load(void);
    settings_load();  // (read once; without the launcher it would come later, in boot)
    if (!getenv("LARECOMP_FPS60")) g_on = g_settings.fps >= 60, g_all60 = false;
    g_rate = g_settings.fps == 120 ? 120 : 60, g_g1 = (uint32_t)(1000000000u / (uint32_t)g_rate);
    extern uint64_t rt_addr(uint64_t eevee);  // (runtime/fnhook.c: 0 in a build it doesn't know)
    if (!rt_addr(FIELD_UPDATE)) g_on = g_all60 = false;
    if (g_on || g_stats || getenv("LARECOMP_INPUT_LOOP")) hook_all();
    // the world's update always: g_played tells the title screen (game_title) whatever the frame rate
    else if (rt_addr(FIELD_UPDATE)) rt_register_fnhook(FIELD_UPDATE, field_hook);
    g_world = true, g_special = g_scene = g_played = false;
    if (g_on) LOG("[fps60] on: the world at %d, menus at 30 with in-between images, battles and captures at 30\n", g_rate);
}

__attribute__((constructor)) static void fps60_init(void) {
    const char *e = getenv("LARECOMP_FPS60");
    g_on = e && atoi(e);
    g_all60 = e && atoi(e) == 2;
    g_stats = getenv("LARECOMP_FPS60_STATS") != NULL;  // (the hooks: fps60_configure)
    if (!g_on && (getenv("LARECOMP_SHOT_REL") || getenv("LARECOMP_WINDOW_SHOTS_REL"))) { rt_register_fnhook(ENCOUNTER_SCENE, scene_start_hook); rt_register_fnhook(BATTLE_START, scene_start_hook); }
    e = getenv("LARECOMP_G1_READERS");
    char buf[512];
    if (!e) return;
    snprintf(buf, sizeof buf, "%s", e);
    for (char *t = strtok(buf, ","); t; t = strtok(NULL, ",")) rt_register_fnhook(strtoull(t, NULL, 16), g1_reader_hook);
}

```

`runtime/hle/fps60_research.c`:

```c
// Research tools of the 60 fps work (docs/PESQUISA-60FPS.md, docs/DEPURACAO.md), kept out of runtime/hle/fps60.c: each
// one is off unless its LARECOMP_* variable is set.
#include <stdatomic.h>
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <math.h>
#include <pthread.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "../hle.h"
#include "../settings.h"

void rt_register_fnhook(uint64_t addr, int (*fn)(Cpu *c, uint64_t addr));  // runtime/fnhook.c
void rt_call_original(Cpu *c, uint64_t addr);
uint64_t renderer_game_frame(void);
uint64_t fps60_timers(void);  // runtime/hle/fps60.c: the frame-step timers (the accessor's x0)

// Research (LARECOMP_ELAPSED_LOG=1): the elapsed time the animation functions f_7000663660 / f_7000664cd0 divide by
// G[index]: the object their parameter holds, asked as they do (its first virtual method, argument 1), field +8.
// LARECOMP_ELAPSED_LOG="<addr>:<which>[,...]" names other readers and the argument they pass (f_7000029d30, the frame
// loop: 0; f_700067be50: 1); LARECOMP_TIME_PROBE_FRAMES limits it to some presents.
static uint64_t g_el_fn[16];
static int g_el_arg[16], g_nel;
static long g_tp_from, g_tp_to = 0x7fffffffL;  // (LARECOMP_TIME_PROBE_FRAMES: shared by the tools below)
static int elapsed_hook(Cpu *c, uint64_t addr) {
    static int n;
    long f = (long)renderer_game_frame();
    if (f < g_tp_from || f > g_tp_to) return 0;
    int which = 1;
    for (int i = 0; i < g_nel; i++) if (g_el_fn[i] == addr) which = g_el_arg[i];
    uint64_t saved[32], pc_arg = c->x[1];
    memcpy(saved, c->x, sizeof saved);
    uint64_t obj = pc_arg ? *(uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)pc_arg : 0;
    if (obj >= 0x7000000000ull && n < 400) {
        uint64_t vt = *(uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)obj, fn = vt >= 0x7000000000ull ? *(uint64_t *)(uintptr_t)vt : 0;
        if (fn >= 0x7000000000ull) {
            c->x[0] = obj;
            c->x[1] = (uint64_t)which;
            guest_call(c, fn);
            uint64_t r = c->x[0];
            if (r >= 0x7000000000ull)
                LOG("[elapsed] f_%llx present %llu: delta %lld ns (timer %d: object %llx, getter f_%llx, step %llx)\n", (unsigned long long)addr,
                    (unsigned long long)renderer_game_frame(), (long long)*(const int64_t *)(uintptr_t)(r + 8), which,
                    (unsigned long long)obj, (unsigned long long)fn, (unsigned long long)r);
            n++;
        }
    }
    memcpy(c->x, saved, sizeof saved);
    return 0;
}

__attribute__((constructor)) static void elapsed_init(void) {
    if (getenv("LARECOMP_ELAPSED_LOG")) {
        const char *fr = getenv("LARECOMP_TIME_PROBE_FRAMES");
        if (fr) { g_tp_from = atol(fr); g_tp_to = strchr(fr, '-') ? atol(strchr(fr, '-') + 1) : g_tp_from; }
        char lb[512];
        snprintf(lb, sizeof lb, "%s", getenv("LARECOMP_ELAPSED_LOG"));
        if (strchr(lb, ':'))
            for (char *t = strtok(lb, ","); t && g_nel < 16; t = strtok(NULL, ",")) {
                g_el_fn[g_nel] = strtoull(t, NULL, 16);
                g_el_arg[g_nel] = strchr(t, ':') ? atoi(strchr(t, ':') + 1) : 1;
                rt_register_fnhook(g_el_fn[g_nel++], elapsed_hook);
            }
        else {
            rt_register_fnhook(0x7000663660ull, elapsed_hook);
            rt_register_fnhook(0x7000664cd0ull, elapsed_hook);
        }
    }
}

// ---- research: LARECOMP_STEP_SCALE="<fn addr of the running build>:<factor>[,...]": timer 1's step times that factor
// while the function runs (which reader of the step a speed comes from: the world's walking at 60 / 120 fps)
#define SS_MAX 8
static uint64_t g_ss_fn[SS_MAX];
static double g_ss_k[SS_MAX];
static int g_nss;
static int step_scale_hook(Cpu *c, uint64_t addr) {
    double k = 1;
    for (int i = 0; i < g_nss; i++) if (g_ss_fn[i] == addr) k = g_ss_k[i];
    volatile int64_t *step = fps60_timers() ? (volatile int64_t *)(uintptr_t)(fps60_timers() + 0x20) : NULL;
    int64_t was = step ? *step : 0;
    static int log = -1, n;  // LARECOMP_STEP_SCALE_LOG=<first present>: the object's +0x494..+0x49c, 40 calls from then
    if (log == -1) log = getenv("LARECOMP_STEP_SCALE_LOG") ? atoi(getenv("LARECOMP_STEP_SCALE_LOG")) : -2;
    if (log >= 0 && (long)renderer_game_frame() >= log && n < 40 && c->x[0] >= 0x7000000000ull) {
        const uint8_t *o = (const uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)c->x[0];
        n++;
        LOG("[stepscale] present %llu f_%llx obj %llx: +494 %u +498 %u +49c %g +493 %u step %lld\n",
            (unsigned long long)renderer_game_frame(), (unsigned long long)addr, (unsigned long long)c->x[0],
            *(const uint32_t *)(o + 0x494), *(const uint32_t *)(o + 0x498), *(const float *)(o + 0x49c), o[0x493], (long long)was);
    }
    if (step) *step = (int64_t)((double)was * k);
    rt_call_original(c, addr);
    if (step) *step = was;
    {   // LARECOMP_FIND_MOVER=<first present>: in each object (its first 0x1000 bytes) handed to the function, the float
        // triples whose ground-plane step (x, z) between two of its updates is 1-20 cm - a walking character's position -
        // for 6 updates; logged with their offsets
        static long from = -2;
        if (from == -2) from = getenv("LARECOMP_FIND_MOVER") ? atol(getenv("LARECOMP_FIND_MOVER")) : -1;
        static struct { uint64_t obj; float prev[0x400]; int hits[0x400]; int n; } fm[32];
        long f = (long)renderer_game_frame();
        uint64_t o = c->x[0];
        if (from >= 0 && f >= from && f < from + 6 && o >= 0x7000000000ull) {
            int i = 0;
            while (i < 32 && fm[i].obj && fm[i].obj != o) i++;
            if (i < 32) {
                const float *now = (const float *)(uintptr_t)o;
                if (fm[i].obj == o && fm[i].n)
                    for (int w = 0; w + 2 < 0x400; w++) {
                        float dx = now[w] - fm[i].prev[w], dz = now[w + 2] - fm[i].prev[w + 2];
                        float d = sqrtf(dx * dx + dz * dz);
                        if (d > 1 && d < 20 && isfinite(d) && fabsf(now[w]) < 1e6f) fm[i].hits[w]++;
                    }
                fm[i].obj = o;
                memcpy(fm[i].prev, now, sizeof fm[i].prev);
                fm[i].n++;
                static FILE *dump;  // LARECOMP_FIND_MOVER_DUMP=<file>: every object's 0x1000 bytes at each of those updates
                static int dump_init;
                if (!dump_init) { dump_init = 1; const char *p = getenv("LARECOMP_FIND_MOVER_DUMP"); if (p) dump = fopen(p, "w"); }
                if (dump) {  // (one write per line, under a lock: several game threads update characters)
                    static pthread_mutex_t lock = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;
                    static char line[0x400 * 9 + 64];
                    pthread_mutex_lock(&lock);
                    int len = snprintf(line, sizeof line, "%ld %llx", f, (unsigned long long)o);
                    for (int w = 0; w < 0x400; w++) len += snprintf(line + len, sizeof line - len, " %08x", ((const uint32_t *)now)[w]);
                    line[len++] = '\n';
                    fwrite(line, 1, (size_t)len, dump);
                    fflush(dump);
                    pthread_mutex_unlock(&lock);
                }
            }
        }
        if (from >= 0 && f == from + 6) {
            for (int i = 0; i < 32 && fm[i].obj; i++)
                for (int w = 0; w + 2 < 0x400; w++)
                    if (fm[i].hits[w] >= 4) {
                        const float *now = (const float *)(uintptr_t)fm[i].obj;
                        LOG("[mover] obj %llx +0x%x: (%g, %g, %g) moved in %d updates\n", (unsigned long long)fm[i].obj, w * 4,
                            now[w], now[w + 1], now[w + 2], fm[i].hits[w]);
                    }
            from = -1;
        }
    }
    return 1;
}
__attribute__((constructor)) static void step_scale_init(void) {
    const char *e = getenv("LARECOMP_STEP_SCALE");
    if (!e) return;
    extern void rt_register_fnhook_raw(uint64_t addr, int (*fn)(Cpu *c, uint64_t addr));
    char buf[512];
    snprintf(buf, sizeof buf, "%s", e);
    for (char *t = strtok(buf, ","); t && g_nss < SS_MAX; t = strtok(NULL, ",")) {
        g_ss_fn[g_nss] = strtoull(t, NULL, 16);
        g_ss_k[g_nss] = strchr(t, ':') ? atof(strchr(t, ':') + 1) : 1;
        rt_register_fnhook_raw(g_ss_fn[g_nss++], step_scale_hook);
    }
}

// ---- research: LARECOMP_FARG_SCALE="<fn addr of the running build>:<factor>[,...]": the function's first float argument
// (s0: a time step handed down) times that factor (which part of an update a speed comes from)
static uint64_t g_fa_fn[SS_MAX];
static float g_fa_k[SS_MAX];
static int g_nfa;
static int farg_scale_hook(Cpu *c, uint64_t addr) {
    float s0;
    memcpy(&s0, &c->v[0], 4);
    static int log = -1, n;  // LARECOMP_FARG_LOG=<first present>: x0's floats +0x120..+0x138 (an animation player's), 300 calls
    if (log == -1) log = getenv("LARECOMP_FARG_LOG") ? atoi(getenv("LARECOMP_FARG_LOG")) : -2;
    if (log >= 0 && (long)renderer_game_frame() >= log && n < 300 && c->x[0] >= 0x7000000000ull) {
        const uint8_t *o = (const uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)c->x[0];
        n++;
        LOG("[farg] present %llu obj %llx dt %g: mode %u fps %u speed %g time %g start %g end %g\n", (unsigned long long)renderer_game_frame(),
            (unsigned long long)c->x[0], s0, *(const uint32_t *)(o + 0x120), *(const uint32_t *)(o + 0x124), *(const float *)(o + 0x128),
            *(const float *)(o + 0x12c), *(const float *)(o + 0x130), *(const float *)(o + 0x134));
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < g_nfa; i++) if (g_fa_fn[i] == addr) s0 *= g_fa_k[i];
    memcpy(&c->v[0], &s0, 4);
    rt_call_original(c, addr);
    return 1;
}
__attribute__((constructor)) static void farg_scale_init(void) {
    const char *e = getenv("LARECOMP_FARG_SCALE");
    if (!e) return;
    extern void rt_register_fnhook_raw(uint64_t addr, int (*fn)(Cpu *c, uint64_t addr));
    char buf[512];
    snprintf(buf, sizeof buf, "%s", e);
    for (char *t = strtok(buf, ","); t && g_nfa < SS_MAX; t = strtok(NULL, ",")) {
        g_fa_fn[g_nfa] = strtoull(t, NULL, 16);
        g_fa_k[g_nfa] = strchr(t, ':') ? (float)atof(strchr(t, ':') + 1) : 1;
        rt_register_fnhook_raw(g_fa_fn[g_nfa++], farg_scale_hook);
    }
}

// ---- research: LARECOMP_FNWATCH=<guest addr of a float> + LARECOMP_FNWATCH_FNS="<fn addr of the running build>[,...]": logs
// (the first 200 times) when the float changes during one of those functions - which one writes it, and by how much
static uint64_t g_watch;
static int watch_hook(Cpu *c, uint64_t addr) {
    static int n;
    volatile float *w = (volatile float *)(uintptr_t)g_watch;
    float before = *w;
    uint64_t x0 = c->x[0];
    float s0;
    memcpy(&s0, &c->v[0], 4);
    rt_call_original(c, addr);
    float after = *w;
    if (after != before && n < 200) {
        n++;
        LOG("[fnwatch] present %llu f_%llx (x0 %llx s0 %g, x0 +0x78 %g): %g -> %g (d %g)\n", (unsigned long long)renderer_game_frame(),
            (unsigned long long)addr, (unsigned long long)x0, s0, x0 >= 0x7000000000ull ? *(const float *)(uintptr_t)(x0 + 0x78) : 0.0f,
            before, after, after - before);
    }
    return 1;
}
__attribute__((constructor)) static void watch_init(void) {
    const char *e = getenv("LARECOMP_FNWATCH"), *fns = getenv("LARECOMP_FNWATCH_FNS");  // (LARECOMP_WATCH: memwatch.c's)
    if (!e || !fns) return;
    g_watch = strtoull(e, NULL, 16);
    extern void rt_register_fnhook_raw(uint64_t addr, int (*fn)(Cpu *c, uint64_t addr));
    char buf[1024];
    snprintf(buf, sizeof buf, "%s", fns);
    for (char *t = strtok(buf, ","); t; t = strtok(NULL, ",")) rt_register_fnhook_raw(strtoull(t, NULL, 16), watch_hook);
}

// ---- research: LARECOMP_TIME_PROBE="<fn addr>[,...]" (+ LARECOMP_TIME_PROBE_FRAMES=<first>-<last>) ------------------
// The readers of the frame-duration table G take an elapsed-time object in x1 (its +8: nanoseconds): log, per call, the
// present, x1's elapsed time and what the function returned (x0, and d0 as a double), up to 600 lines.
static int time_probe_hook(Cpu *c, uint64_t addr) {
    static int lines;
    uint64_t x1 = c->x[1];
    long f = (long)renderer_game_frame();
    int64_t el = x1 >= 0x7000000000ull && x1 < 0x7800000000ull ? *(const int64_t *)(uintptr_t)(x1 + 8) : -1;
    rt_call_original(c, addr);
    if (f >= g_tp_from && f <= g_tp_to && lines < 600) {
        double d0;
        memcpy(&d0, &c->v[0], 8);
        LOG("[time] present %ld f_%llx elapsed %lld ns -> x0 %llx d0 %g\n", f, (unsigned long long)addr, (long long)el,
            (unsigned long long)c->x[0], d0);
        lines++;
    }
    return 1;
}
__attribute__((constructor)) static void time_probe_init(void) {
    const char *e = getenv("LARECOMP_TIME_PROBE");
    if (!e) return;
    const char *fr = getenv("LARECOMP_TIME_PROBE_FRAMES");
    if (fr) { g_tp_from = atol(fr); g_tp_to = strchr(fr, '-') ? atol(strchr(fr, '-') + 1) : g_tp_from; }
    char buf[512];
    snprintf(buf, sizeof buf, "%s", e);
    for (char *t = strtok(buf, ","); t; t = strtok(NULL, ",")) rt_register_fnhook(strtoull(t, NULL, 16), time_probe_hook);
}

// ---- research: LARECOMP_TIMER_USERS=<first>-<last> -------------------------------------------------------------
// Who reads the frame-step timers: calls to their getter f_70000395f0 (x1 = the timer, the caller's lr), counted over
// those presents and listed at the last one. Timer 1 is the step the accessor f_7000039600 rewrites every frame with
// G[1]; timer 0 keeps 33.3 ms.
#define TIMER_GETTER 0x70000395f0ull
static struct { uint64_t lr; int which; uint64_t n; } g_tu[256];
static int g_ntu;
static long g_tu_from, g_tu_to;
static int timer_users_hook(Cpu *c, uint64_t addr) {
    long f = (long)renderer_game_frame();
    if (f >= g_tu_from && f <= g_tu_to) {
        uint64_t lr = c->x[30];
        int which = (int)c->x[1], i;
        for (i = 0; i < g_ntu && !(g_tu[i].lr == lr && g_tu[i].which == which); i++) {}
        if (i == g_ntu && g_ntu < 256) g_tu[g_ntu++] = (__typeof__(g_tu[0])){lr, which, 0};
        if (i < 256) g_tu[i].n++;
    } else if (f > g_tu_to && g_ntu) {
        for (int i = 0; i < g_ntu; i++)
            LOG("[timers] timer %d read from lr %llx: %llu times in %ld presents\n", g_tu[i].which, (unsigned long long)g_tu[i].lr,
                (unsigned long long)g_tu[i].n, g_tu_to - g_tu_from + 1);
        g_ntu = 0;
        g_tu_to = -1;
    }
    (void)addr;
    return 0;
}
__attribute__((constructor)) static void timer_users_init(void) {
    const char *e = getenv("LARECOMP_TIMER_USERS");
    if (!e) return;
    g_tu_from = atol(e);
    g_tu_to = strchr(e, '-') ? atol(strchr(e, '-') + 1) : g_tu_from;
    rt_register_fnhook(TIMER_GETTER, timer_users_hook);
}

// ---- research: LARECOMP_CALLCOUNT="<fn>[,...]" (+ LARECOMP_TIME_PROBE_FRAMES): calls per present of each function
#define CC_MAX 8
static uint64_t g_cc_fn[CC_MAX];
static unsigned g_cc_n[CC_MAX];
static int g_ncc;
static long g_cc_frame = -1;
static int callcount_hook(Cpu *c, uint64_t addr) {
    long f = (long)renderer_game_frame();
    if (f != g_cc_frame) {
        if (g_cc_frame >= g_tp_from && g_cc_frame <= g_tp_to) {
            char line[256];
            int o = snprintf(line, sizeof line, "[calls] present %ld:", g_cc_frame);
            for (int i = 0; i < g_ncc; i++) o += snprintf(line + o, sizeof line - o, " f_%llx %u", (unsigned long long)g_cc_fn[i], g_cc_n[i]);
            LOG("%s\n", line);
        }
        memset(g_cc_n, 0, sizeof g_cc_n);
        g_cc_frame = f;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < g_ncc; i++) if (g_cc_fn[i] == addr) g_cc_n[i]++;
    (void)c;
    return 0;
}
__attribute__((constructor)) static void callcount_init(void) {
    const char *e = getenv("LARECOMP_CALLCOUNT");
    if (!e) return;
    const char *fr = getenv("LARECOMP_TIME_PROBE_FRAMES");
    if (fr) { g_tp_from = atol(fr); g_tp_to = strchr(fr, '-') ? atol(strchr(fr, '-') + 1) : g_tp_from; }
    char buf[512];
    snprintf(buf, sizeof buf, "%s", e);
    for (char *t = strtok(buf, ","); t && g_ncc < CC_MAX; t = strtok(NULL, ",")) {
        g_cc_fn[g_ncc++] = strtoull(t, NULL, 16);
        rt_register_fnhook(g_cc_fn[g_ncc - 1], callcount_hook);
    }
}

// ---- research: LARECOMP_PROBE="<fn addr>[:<bytes>]" ----------------------------------------------------------------
// At each entry of the function, remember its x0 (object) and, after the original returns, x0 (result): for the next
// LARECOMP_PROBE_FRAMES (120) presents, compare `bytes` (0x400) of each of them with the previous present and log, at
// the end, every 32-bit word that changed: how many presents, and its usual step as an integer and as a float. A
// frame counter shows as an integer stepping by 1 (or a float by a constant) every present of the scene.
#define PROBE_MAX 4
static struct { uint64_t base; const char *what; uint32_t prev[0x400 / 4]; uint32_t changed[0x400 / 4]; int32_t step[0x400 / 4]; uint32_t step_n[0x400 / 4]; bool have; } g_probe[PROBE_MAX];
static int g_nprobe;
static uint32_t g_probe_bytes = 0x400;
static uint64_t g_probe_from, g_probe_to;
static int probe_hook(Cpu *c, uint64_t addr) {
    uint64_t obj = c->x[0];
    rt_call_original(c, addr);
    uint64_t ret = c->x[0];
    if (!g_probe_from) g_probe_from = renderer_game_frame() + 1, g_probe_to = g_probe_from + (getenv("LARECOMP_PROBE_FRAMES") ? atoi(getenv("LARECOMP_PROBE_FRAMES")) : 120);
    for (int pass = 0; pass < 2 && g_nprobe < PROBE_MAX; pass++) {
        uint64_t p = pass ? ret : obj;
        if (p < 0x7000000000ull || p > 0x7800000000ull) continue;
        g_probe[g_nprobe].base = p, g_probe[g_nprobe].what = pass ? "returned object" : "x0 object";
        LOG("[probe] f_%llx %s %llx\n", (unsigned long long)addr, g_probe[g_nprobe].what, (unsigned long long)p);
        g_nprobe++;
    }
    return 1;
}
void fps60_probe_present(void) {
    uint64_t f = renderer_game_frame();
    if (!g_probe_from || f < g_probe_from || f > g_probe_to) return;
    for (int i = 0; i < g_nprobe; i++) {
        const uint32_t *now = (const uint32_t *)(uintptr_t)g_probe[i].base;
        for (uint32_t w = 0; w < g_probe_bytes / 4; w++) {
            if (g_probe[i].have && now[w] != g_probe[i].prev[w]) {
                g_probe[i].changed[w]++;
                int32_t d = (int32_t)(now[w] - g_probe[i].prev[w]);
                if (d == g_probe[i].step[w]) g_probe[i].step_n[w]++;
                else if (g_probe[i].step_n[w] == 0) g_probe[i].step[w] = d;
            }
            g_probe[i].prev[w] = now[w];
        }
        g_probe[i].have = true;
    }
    if (f == g_probe_to) {
        for (int i = 0; i < g_nprobe; i++)
            for (uint32_t w = 0; w < g_probe_bytes / 4; w++) {
                if (g_probe[i].changed[w] < 5) continue;
                float fv;
                memcpy(&fv, &g_probe[i].prev[w], 4);
                LOG("[probe] %s +0x%03x: changed in %u of %llu presents; usual step %d (%u times) value %u / %g\n", g_probe[i].what, w * 4,
                    g_probe[i].changed[w], (unsigned long long)(g_probe_to - g_probe_from), g_probe[i].step[w], g_probe[i].step_n[w],
                    g_probe[i].prev[w], fv);
            }
    }
}
__attribute__((constructor)) static void probe_init(void) {
    const char *e = getenv("LARECOMP_PROBE");
    if (!e) return;
    char buf[128];
    snprintf(buf, sizeof buf, "%s", e);
    char *colon = strchr(buf, ':');
    if (colon) *colon = 0, g_probe_bytes = (uint32_t)strtoul(colon + 1, NULL, 16);
    if (g_probe_bytes > 0x400) g_probe_bytes = 0x400;
    rt_register_fnhook(strtoull(buf, NULL, 16), probe_hook);
}
```

`runtime/hle/framepace.c`:

```c
// Frame pacing: the game's speed doesn't depend on the frame rate.
// The game advances its world each frame by its frame period (16.67 ms) times the swap interval its frame timer
// (f_700000c910) reads from the system object - normally 1. When a frame takes longer than a vsync (GPU-bound at
// 32:9, a hitch), the next frame starts a vsync later but still advanced only 16.67 ms: slow motion (30 fps = half
// speed). tools/patches.py FRAME_STEPS_SITE routes that read here: we return how many vsyncs really passed since
// the last frame, so the world advances by the time that passed. The game's own waiting is unaffected (it reads
// the interval nowhere else). Shared by the macOS and Windows builds.
// FINDING (2026-10-09): forcing 2 steps did NOT change Link's walking speed - gameplay is a true fixed step per
// frame; this timer feeds something else. Kept for research, off by default.
//   LARECOMP_FRAMEPACE=1     hand the timer the vsyncs elapsed (default: the game's own value)
//   LARECOMP_FRAME_STEPS_MAX maximum steps per frame (default 4: after a long stall the game doesn't jump ahead)
//   LARECOMP_FORCE_STEPS=<n> (test) always n
#include <stdlib.h>

#include "../hle.h"

extern volatile uint64_t g_vsync_count;  // runtime/hle/vi.c
uint64_t g_frame_steps_late;             // (stats) frames that advanced more than one step

uint32_t rt_frame_steps(uint32_t interval) {
    static int on = -1, max_steps, forced;
    if (on < 0) {
        const char *e = ENV("LARECOMP_FRAMEPACE");
        on = e ? atoi(e) != 0 : 0;  // off by default: the world (Link's movement) doesn't use this step (tested)
        e = ENV("LARECOMP_FRAME_STEPS_MAX");
        max_steps = e ? atoi(e) : 4;
        if (max_steps < 1) max_steps = 1;
        e = ENV("LARECOMP_FORCE_STEPS");
        forced = e ? atoi(e) : 0;
    }
    static int ncall;
    if (ENV("LARECOMP_LOG_FRAMEPACE") && ncall++ % 120 == 0) LOG("[framepace] call %d interval %u vsync %llu\n", ncall, interval, (unsigned long long)g_vsync_count);
    if (forced > 0) return (uint32_t)forced;
    static uint64_t last;
    uint64_t now = __atomic_load_n(&g_vsync_count, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
    uint64_t steps = last ? now - last : 1;
    last = now;
    if (!on) return interval;
    if (steps < interval) steps = interval;  // (the game's own 30 fps mode: it waits that many vsyncs anyway)
    if (steps < 1) steps = 1;
    if (steps > (uint64_t)max_steps) steps = (uint64_t)max_steps;
    if (steps > 1) g_frame_steps_late++;
    return (uint32_t)steps;
}
```

`runtime/hle/heaps.c`:

```c
// Game heaps (engine limits). The game carves its memory into SDK heaps of fixed sizes: nn::mem::StandardAllocator
// (general), nn::lmem unit heaps (fixed-size blocks: object pools) and frame heaps. A heap that runs out returns
// NULL and the game crashes further on (bushsanity: ~450 actors around Link -> null weak_ptr in f_70010d0f00).
// These wrappers call the SDK's own implementation (loader_find_symbol), log heap creation (LARECOMP_LOG_HEAPS=1)
// and every allocation that fails (once per caller), and can grow heaps (heap_scale) - a recomp has memory to spare.
#include <pthread.h>
#ifdef _WIN32
#include <malloc.h>
#endif
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "../hle.h"

uint64_t loader_find_symbol(const char *name);
void guest_call(Cpu *c, uint64_t addr);

static uint64_t orig(const char *name, uint64_t *cache) {
    if (!*cache) *cache = loader_find_symbol(name);
    if (!*cache) FATAL("heaps: no SDK implementation of %s\n", name);
    return *cache;
}

static void fail_once(const char *what, uint64_t lr, uint64_t size) {
    static uint64_t seen[64];
    static int n;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) if (seen[i] == lr) return;
    if (n < 64) seen[n++] = lr;
    LOG("[heaps] %s FAILED (size %#llx) from lr %llx\n", what, (unsigned long long)size, (unsigned long long)lr);
}

#define CALL(sym)                                    \
    do {                                             \
        static uint64_t a_;                          \
        uint64_t lr_ = c->x[30];                     \
        guest_call(c, orig(sym, &a_));               \
        c->x[30] = lr_;                              \
    } while (0)

// Unit heaps are fixed pools (e.g. 256 x 0x50-byte objects per loaded area: bushsanity's extra actors ran out at
// ~450 actors around Link). Every unit heap gets UNIT_SCALE times the units in a buffer of ours (the game's own
// buffer stays unused); freed again in DestroyUnitHeap. LARECOMP_UNIT_HEAP_SCALE overrides (1 = the game's sizes).
typedef struct { uint64_t head; void *mem; } UnitBuf;
static UnitBuf g_unit[256];
static pthread_mutex_t g_unit_lock = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;

// Reboot: our unit-heap buffers (host memory, not in the guest window) go with the game that made them.
RT_ON_RESET(heaps_reset) {
    for (int i = 0; i < 256; i++)
        if (g_unit[i].mem) {
#ifdef _WIN32
            _aligned_free(g_unit[i].mem);
#else
            free(g_unit[i].mem);
#endif
            g_unit[i].mem = NULL;
        }
}

static int unit_scale(void) {
    static int s = -1;
    if (s < 0) { const char *e = ENV("LARECOMP_UNIT_HEAP_SCALE"); s = e ? atoi(e) : 4; if (s < 1) s = 1; }
    return s;
}

// nn::lmem::CreateUnitHeap(void *addr, size_t size, size_t unit, int align, int opt, HeapHead *head)
HLE_FUNC("_ZN2nn4lmem14CreateUnitHeapEPvmmiiPNS0_6detail8HeapHeadE", heap_create_unit) {
    uint64_t lr = c->x[30], size = c->x[1], unit = c->x[2];
    int k = unit_scale();
    void *mem = NULL;
    if (k > 1 && unit) {
        uint64_t big = size * (uint64_t)k;
#ifdef _WIN32
        mem = _aligned_malloc(big, 0x1000);
        if (mem) {
#else
        if (posix_memalign(&mem, 0x1000, big) == 0) {
#endif
            memset(mem, 0, big);
            c->x[0] = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)mem;
            c->x[1] = big;
        } else {
            mem = NULL;
        }
    }
    uint64_t head = c->x[5];
    CALL("_ZN2nn4lmem14CreateUnitHeapEPvmmiiPNS0_6detail8HeapHeadE");
    if (mem) {
        pthread_mutex_lock(&g_unit_lock);
        for (int i = 0; i < 256; i++)
            if (!g_unit[i].mem) { g_unit[i].head = c->x[0] ? c->x[0] : head; g_unit[i].mem = mem; break; }
        pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_unit_lock);
    }
    if (ENV("LARECOMP_LOG_HEAPS"))
        LOG("[heaps] unit heap %#llx bytes, unit %#llx (%llu units, x%d) from lr %llx -> %llx\n", (unsigned long long)size,
            (unsigned long long)unit, unit ? (unsigned long long)(size / unit) : 0ull, mem ? k : 1, (unsigned long long)lr,
            (unsigned long long)c->x[0]);
}

HLE_FUNC("_ZN2nn4lmem15DestroyUnitHeapEPNS0_6detail8HeapHeadE", heap_destroy_unit) {
    uint64_t head = c->x[0];
    CALL("_ZN2nn4lmem15DestroyUnitHeapEPNS0_6detail8HeapHeadE");
    pthread_mutex_lock(&g_unit_lock);
    for (int i = 0; i < 256; i++)
        if (g_unit[i].mem && g_unit[i].head == head) {
#ifdef _WIN32
            _aligned_free(g_unit[i].mem);
#else
            free(g_unit[i].mem);
#endif
            g_unit[i].mem = NULL;
            break;
        }
    pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_unit_lock);
}

HLE_FUNC("_ZN2nn4lmem20AllocateFromUnitHeapEPNS0_6detail8HeapHeadE", heap_alloc_unit) {
    uint64_t lr = c->x[30], head = c->x[0];
    CALL("_ZN2nn4lmem20AllocateFromUnitHeapEPNS0_6detail8HeapHeadE");
    if (!c->x[0]) fail_once("unit heap allocation", lr, head);
}

// nn::lmem::CreateFrameHeap(void *addr, size_t size, int opt)
HLE_FUNC("_ZN2nn4lmem15CreateFrameHeapEPvmi", heap_create_frame) {
    uint64_t lr = c->x[30], size = c->x[1];
    CALL("_ZN2nn4lmem15CreateFrameHeapEPvmi");
    if (ENV("LARECOMP_LOG_HEAPS"))
        LOG("[heaps] frame heap %#llx bytes from lr %llx\n", (unsigned long long)size, (unsigned long long)lr);
}

HLE_FUNC("_ZN2nn4lmem21AllocateFromFrameHeapEPNS0_6detail8HeapHeadEmi", heap_alloc_frame) {
    uint64_t lr = c->x[30], size = c->x[1];
    CALL("_ZN2nn4lmem21AllocateFromFrameHeapEPNS0_6detail8HeapHeadEmi");
    if (!c->x[0]) fail_once("frame heap allocation", lr, size);
}

// nn::mem::StandardAllocator::Initialize(void *addr, size_t size[, bool])
HLE_FUNC("_ZN2nn3mem17StandardAllocator10InitializeEPvm", heap_std_init) {
    uint64_t lr = c->x[30], size = c->x[2];
    CALL("_ZN2nn3mem17StandardAllocator10InitializeEPvm");
    if (ENV("LARECOMP_LOG_HEAPS"))
        LOG("[heaps] standard allocator %#llx bytes from lr %llx\n", (unsigned long long)size, (unsigned long long)lr);
}

HLE_FUNC("_ZN2nn3mem17StandardAllocator10InitializeEPvmb", heap_std_init_b) {
    uint64_t lr = c->x[30], size = c->x[2];
    CALL("_ZN2nn3mem17StandardAllocator10InitializeEPvmb");
    if (ENV("LARECOMP_LOG_HEAPS"))
        LOG("[heaps] standard allocator %#llx bytes (b) from lr %llx\n", (unsigned long long)size, (unsigned long long)lr);
}

HLE_FUNC("_ZN2nn3mem17StandardAllocator8AllocateEm", heap_std_alloc) {
    uint64_t lr = c->x[30], size = c->x[1];
    CALL("_ZN2nn3mem17StandardAllocator8AllocateEm");
    if (!c->x[0] && size) fail_once("standard allocation", lr, size);
}

HLE_FUNC("_ZN2nn3mem17StandardAllocator8AllocateEmm", heap_std_alloc_a) {
    uint64_t lr = c->x[30], size = c->x[1];
    CALL("_ZN2nn3mem17StandardAllocator8AllocateEmm");
    if (!c->x[0] && size) fail_once("standard allocation (aligned)", lr, size);
}
```
